body:
## Can I try it before talking to anyone?

Yes. A live demo runs at [boiler-erp.ahromlabs.com](https://boiler-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo) with a made-up company, Acme Boilers, and sample orders already moving through design, procurement, stores, production, QC and dispatch. Leave a name and email, pick a department head to log in as, and use the real screens: open a project, raise a purchase request, download a purchase order or packing list PDF. Emails and WhatsApp are switched off, and the data resets every night, so nothing you do there reaches anyone.

## What does a boiler manufacturer need that a generic ERP doesn't give?

Four things generic ERPs treat as edge cases are the core of this business. Every boiler is its own project, with its own bill of materials and a chain of milestones across design, procurement, stores, production, QC, dispatch and commissioning. Every plate and tube has to trace back to the [material test certificate](/systems/material-test-certificate) it arrived with. Every unit ships with statutory paperwork for the Directorate of Boilers under the Indian Boiler Regulations. And steel plate is bought in standard sizes and cut, so stock is pieces with dimensions, not a count. The system Ahrom Labs built for [a boiler and pressure-vessel manufacturer](/work#boiler-manufacturer) is designed around those four facts rather than bolted onto a generic stock-and-invoice model.

## Can the IBR statutory folder come out of the system instead of being typed?

Yes, in a few minutes instead of typing it up by hand. The folder — covering letter, Forms II(1), III, III A and IV A under IBR 1950 numbering (Form I Part B, IV Part A, IV Part B and V Part B under [IBR 2026](/ibr/forms)) — comes out of the system, with the form set chosen by boiler model and every part linked to its material test certificate from the bank. A person adds the parts to the folder in a few minutes per boiler; the bill of materials kept for buying and production doesn't fill the forms reliably on its own. Certificate PDFs are read by AI on upload, and matching a certificate to the part it covers is suggested by confidence but always confirmed by a person, because it ends up in paperwork an inspector relies on. The details are in [Keeping test certificates for a boiler's IBR folder](/notes/ibr-statutory-folder-from-bom).

## How is material traced from test certificate to finished boiler?

Each test certificate is identified by certificate, cast and plate number together — one certificate number covered four casts in the client's own sample — and one certificate is typically used across several boilers. When a plate is cut, every used piece, remnant and scrap piece is chained to the plate it came from. QC records heat and lot numbers, non-conformance reports with a disposition and a verification step before closing, and hold points that stop a job until inspection clears it.

The heat number and certificate are captured once, when a plate is received, and every piece cut from it inherits them automatically — nobody re-types them at the cutting table. A non-conformance can be dispositioned as rework, repair, scrap or use-as-is: rework and repair open a new job card that carries the lineage of the original, and scrap or use-as-is can't be saved without a written justification. Hold points come from the work order's own route — a step marked as a quality checkpoint holds the job until QC releases it — so there is no separate inspection plan to keep in step with production.

Shops that also build to the ASME Code need the same trail for its material rules: see [material test reports and heat numbers](/asme/mtr), and [ASME vs IBR 2026](/asme/asme-vs-ibr) for where the two codes meet. Exporters to the US can start with what a buyer there checks ([buying ASME equipment from India](/asme/buying-from-india)), the [sections of the ASME Code](/asme/bpvc-sections) and [Section IX welder qualification](/asme/section-ix).

## How does work move between departments without chasing people?

Each project's milestones declare what they depend on, and the system shows what each one is waiting for, computed fresh every time the page is opened. Procurement runs as a visible pipeline — requests, sourcing, supplier selection, purchase order issued, closed — with new-item requests from engineering accepted into procurement rather than appearing unannounced. On the shop floor, work orders and job cards carry production; engineering has its own calculation sheets linked to the drawings they substantiate.

## What did each boiler actually cost, and what did we make on it?

Once a sale order has its project, the system shows its actual cost against its selling price. Material cost is the sum of purchase orders actually issued against that project — drafts and cancelled orders don't count as spend. Labour cost is the time logged on the project's job cards multiplied by each employee's cost rate. Margin is the sale order value minus both. When nothing has been bought or logged yet, material and labour show as empty rather than as an estimate.

Work orders carry a planned cost as well as an actual one: planned material from the quantities and unit costs on the work order, planned labour from each route step's planned minutes and the workstation's machine-hour rate. The gap between the two is the Production Cost Variance report. For management, Project Profitability and Customer Profitability run the same costing across every order in a period, so there is one calculation of margin, not three that disagree.

Costing is only as complete as its inputs. Purchase orders and job-card time are counted; outside job work is listed but not priced, overheads aren't allocated yet, and a margin is only real once purchasing and time logging are actually happening in the system.

## What can the owner see across all orders?

Each department has its own reports, and the management reports reuse those numbers rather than recalculating them:

- **Project and customer profitability** — material and labour against selling value, per order and per customer.
- **Manufacturing performance** — work-order throughput, rejection rate, material yield and cost variance.
- **Procurement spend** — by supplier, with a six-month spend trend and each supplier's win rate on quotes.
- **Working capital** — cash plus receivables plus inventory, minus payables.
- **Production** — work order register, rework and rejection, material and labour utilisation, and material shortage against open work orders.
- **Sales** — leads, conversion rate and follow-up completion per salesperson.

The management reports export to PDF from the same computation the screen shows. Machine downtime and OEE are deliberately left out: no machine data is collected, so there would be nothing honest to report.

## Which installed boilers are due for service, and are contracts being renewed?

After commissioning, each boiler stays in the system as the equipment its service calls and contracts attach to. A service call carries a priority and a response time in hours, and moves from open to assigned, in progress, resolved and closed; the resolved and closed times are stamped by the system at the moment the status changes, so response times can't be edited after the fact. Every site visit is logged against its call.

A service contract records its coverage window, visit frequency and what is covered. Renewing one creates a new contract linked to the old one rather than overwriting it, so the history of what was covered, and when, survives. Four reports come off that data: commissioning progress and delay reasons; service calls by priority with response-time compliance; each technician's calls and average resolution time; and active contracts, contracts expiring in the next 30 days, and the renewal rate.

## What happens to plate offcuts?

They go back into stock as real pieces with dimensions, and every weight is derived from geometry rather than typed. In a live test, a 157.00 kg plate became 127.17 kg of parts, a 15.70 kg remnant returned to stock, and 14.13 kg of scrap — summing exactly to the source. When a BOM is released, a fitting remnant is reserved before anything is bought. See [Putting steel plate offcuts back into stock](/notes/plate-remnants-back-into-stock).

## Can GST, TDS and accounts live in the same system?

They do here. The system is the book of record — ledger, GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B, input-tax-credit reconciliation, TDS, reverse charge, fixed assets, bank reconciliation, a books lock and an audit log — with Tally available as an optional sync target. The original plan left regulated accounting to a separate ERP package; in August 2026 that was reversed, and the operations system became the book of record. See [GST, TDS and the general ledger inside a manufacturing ERP](/notes/accounting-inside-the-manufacturing-erp).

GST, TDS, income-tax, professional-tax and PF/ESI rates aren't typed in per company: the system pulls them daily from a central registry where each change is checked against the actual notification and approved by a person before it goes live — see [Keeping GST, TDS and income-tax rates current across every system](/notes/statutory-rates-across-systems). The government's GSTR-2B is imported from the portal's download, with each line's accept or reject status recorded. For dispatch, an e-way bill client that talks directly to the government's NIC system is built to the official specification and goes live once the company's NIC account is set up.

## What does the customer see?

A read-only portal: each order as a stepper from order received to commissioning, with overall progress, estimated dispatch, and the QC certificates and packing lists filed under the stage they belong to. A customer only ever sees their own orders.

## Can it stop drawings leaving the office on a USB drive?

The same system runs a device-control layer on office PCs. USB drives, CDs and DVDs, phones and chosen websites are blocked by default; an employee's attempt to use one files a request, a manager approves it with a one-time code, and access opens for a time-boxed window — 15 minutes by default. Every step is audited.

## What modules does a boiler manufacturer's ERP need?

One per department, sharing the same records rather than handing spreadsheets between them. In the system built for that manufacturer:

- **Sales and CRM** — leads, quotations, sale orders and a payment tracker with stages per order.
- **Engineering** — a multi-level bill of materials with where-used and common/uncommon views, engineering change notes, reusable structure templates, drawings approved by role, and calculation sheets linked to the drawings they substantiate.
- **Procurement** — requests from engineering accepted into a sourcing pipeline, supplier quotes compared side by side, purchase orders with delivery lots, and purchase returns.
- **Stores** — delivery-by-delivery receiving, piece-level plate and section stock with remnants, material indents and gate passes.
- **Production** — work orders above job cards, routed per unit when one order covers several boilers.
- **Quality** — incoming, finished-goods, sub-assembly and job-work inspection, instrument calibration, non-conformance reports with disposition, hold points, and the test-certificate bank behind the IBR folder.
- **Dispatch** — packing lists that need both QC and Production sign-off, freight cost and e-way bill details captured against the invoice.
- **Accounts** — ledger, GST returns, TDS, reverse charge, fixed assets and bank reconciliation, with 23 reports.
- **Installation** — service calls with priorities and response times, service contracts, and service reports.

## Can existing Excel records come across?

Yes, and they were. Bills of materials are imported from the plant's own spreadsheets into the BOM tree, with each line categorised automatically — and when a person corrects a misspelled item once, the import remembers it. Five years of order and payment history came across from the existing Excel tracker and were checked field by field against the sheet, with zero mismatches, before anyone relied on them.

## Should a boiler maker buy an engineering ERP package or build custom?

Engineering ERP packages exist with hundreds of installations, and if one fits your processes with little customisation, it will be cheaper and faster. The system was scoped against one such package's feature list, item by item — then built custom, because the parts that matter most here (the IBR folder built from a bank of test certificates, piece-level plate traceability, a customer portal filed by boiler stage) aren't what packages are built around. The trade-offs in general are in [Tally, ERPNext, Odoo or a custom ERP](/notes/tally-vs-erpnext-vs-custom-erp).

## What should a boiler maker ask any software vendor?

Whoever builds or sells it, these five questions separate a system that fits from one that gets worked around:

1. **Where does money leak today?** Late quotations, cost overruns, slow collections or unbilled service work — the system should be designed around the biggest one first.
2. **Can it show the real cost of one boiler?** Material and labour against selling price, per order, from the purchase orders and job cards themselves — not from a spreadsheet kept on the side.
3. **Can it produce the statutory and quality paperwork from its own records?** The IBR forms, test certificates, inspection results and non-conformances, traced to the parts they cover.
4. **What happens after dispatch?** Service calls, visits and contracts against the specific boiler, with renewals that keep their history.
5. **Who owns the system and the data?** The code, the server and the records — and what it takes to change something next year. Our answer is in [Working with Ahrom Labs](/engagement).

## IBR terms, in one place

The Indian Boiler Regulations, 2026 renumbered the folder's forms on 1 October 2026. The client's folders were filed under the IBR 1950 names, given in brackets; every form and its old name is on [the IBR 2026 forms list](/ibr/forms).

- **[Form I Part B](/ibr/forms/form-i-part-b) (was Form II(1))** — the inspection certificate: inspecting authority, pressures, hydraulic test pressure and date, drawing numbers and signatories.
- **[Form IV Part A](/ibr/forms/form-iv-part-a) (was Form III)** — the boiler's description: dimensions, pressures, heating surface, evaporation, parts manufactured, construction and seams.
- **[Form IV Part B](/ibr/forms/form-iv-part-b) (was Form III-A)** — the certificate for pipes; in the client's folders, a material table for one named part such as the feed pipeline, with steel-making process and heat treatment.
- **[Form V Part B](/ibr/forms/form-v-part-b) (was Form IV-A)** — the extract of every material test certificate used in the boiler, grouped into lettered sections.
- **[Form XXII](/ibr/forms/form-xxii) (was Form XVII)** — the certificate of manufacture and test for a small industrial boiler.
- **Material test certificate (MTC)** — the mill's certificate for a plate, tube or forging, identified here by certificate, cast and plate number together.
- **Hold point** — a stage production can't pass until QC clears it.
- **NCR** — a non-conformance report, closed only after a disposition and a separate QC verification.

## Boundary

Nesting — planning the layout of several parts on one plate — is not part of the system. E-invoicing is researched and deferred. Quotations are priced from default and customer price lists; there is no configurator that builds a price from a boiler's specification, and a pre-sale cost estimate was deliberately left out, because nothing real exists to cost before an order becomes a project. Welding is tracked as a job-card operation, not joint by joint — there is no weld map, WPS or welder-qualification record, or NDT result linked to a joint yet. Remote monitoring of installed boilers (sensors, IoT, SCADA) is not part of this system. The generated IBR forms have been checked against the client's real filed documents; the remaining gaps are formatting, and are being closed form by form.

Yes. Leave a name and email, pick a department head to log in as, and use the real screens in dollars, imperial units and US dates. The data resets every night, so nothing you do there reaches anyone.

## What does an ASME boiler shop need that a generic ERP doesn't give?

Four things a generic ERP treats as edge cases are the core of this business. Every boiler or vessel is its own job, with its own bill of materials and milestones across design, purchasing, receiving, production, QC, shipping and startup. Every plate and tube has to trace back to its [mill test report and heat number](/asme/mtr). Every unit ships with a code record package that an [Authorized Inspector](/asme/authorized-inspector) signs off. And steel plate is bought in standard sizes and cut, so stock is pieces with dimensions, not a count. The system is built around those four facts rather than bolted onto a generic stock-and-invoice model.

## Can the ASME data report package come out of the system?

Yes. The job's QC folder prints the ASME record package from the records kept while the job was built: the data report ([Form P-2](/asme/data-reports) for a Section I firetube boiler, Form U-1A for a Section VIII vessel), the weld map with each welder's stamp, the [WPS and PQR](/asme/wps-pqr-wpq) behind each weld, [welder continuity under QW-322](/asme/welder-continuity) (six months per process), the MTRs by heat number, NDE, [post-weld heat treatment](/asme/pwht) and the [hydrostatic test](/asme/hydrostatic-test). Nobody retypes heat numbers or welder stamps into a separate document; the package is a view of what QC and the shop floor already recorded.

## How is material traced from mill test report to finished boiler?

The heat number and mill test report are captured once, when a plate or tube is received, and every piece cut from it inherits them, so nobody re-types them at the cutting table. When a plate is cut, every used piece, remnant and scrap piece is chained to the plate it came from. Receiving inspection can fail a lot and open an NCR; an NCR is dispositioned as rework, repair, scrap or use-as-is, and scrap or use-as-is can't be saved without a written justification. Hold points come from the work order's own route, so a step marked as a quality checkpoint holds the job until QC releases it.

## Does it work with QuickBooks Online?

Yes. QuickBooks Online stays the books, and the operations system sends it what accounting needs. The shop connects its QuickBooks company once (Intuit sign-in), and its accounts are mapped to the system's accounts, with suggested matches reviewed before they are saved. After that, an invoice goes to QuickBooks with its customer when it is issued, and a payment when it is recorded; on the purchasing side, a vendor bill goes when it is approved and a bill payment when it is made. Each send carries a request id, so a retry never creates a duplicate, and a failure is shown on the invoice or bill with its reason and a Retry button. Sales tax is left to QuickBooks' automated sales tax: each line is sent as taxable or not with the ship-to address, and QuickBooks' total is shown beside ours. In the demo it is connected to an Intuit sandbox company. For the wider picture see [connecting QuickBooks Online to a shop system](/manufacturing/quickbooks-integration).

## What did each job actually cost, and what did we make on it?

Each sales order's job shows actual cost against its selling price. Material cost is the sum of purchase orders actually issued for that job; drafts and canceled orders don't count. Labor cost is the time logged on the job's job cards multiplied by each employee's cost rate. Margin is the order value minus both. Work orders carry a planned cost as well, from planned quantities and each route step's planned minutes at the work center's machine-hour rate, so the variance between planned and actual is a report rather than a spreadsheet. Job profitability and customer profitability run the same costing across every job in a period. See [estimated vs actual job costing](/manufacturing/quickbooks-job-costing) for how this compares with costing inside QuickBooks.

## How does sales tax work?

One sales tax amount per invoice line. In the demo, Ohio customers are taxed and out-of-state shipments are at 0%, and a line can be marked non-taxable. When QuickBooks Online is connected, its automated sales tax works the tax out from the ship-to address. [How an ERP should handle US sales tax](/sales-tax/sales-tax-in-erp) covers nexus, exemption certificates and what to check in any system.

## What happens to plate offcuts?

They go back into stock as real pieces with dimensions, and every weight is derived from geometry rather than typed. In a live test, a 346.1 lb plate became 280.4 lb of parts, a 34.6 lb remnant returned to stock and 31.2 lb of scrap, summing exactly to the source. When a BOM is released, a fitting remnant is reserved before anything is bought. Dimensions are entered and shown in inches and pounds by default, with a Units setting for metric. See [Putting steel plate offcuts back into stock](/notes/plate-remnants-back-into-stock).

## What can the owner see across all jobs?

An executive view of active jobs, value in progress, cash collected and outstanding by customer, with any job running late flagged with its reason. Under it, each department's reports: job and customer profitability, production throughput, rejection rate and cost variance, purchasing spend by supplier with each supplier's win rate on quotes, working capital, and sales conversion per salesperson. The management reports export to PDF from the same calculation the screen shows.

## Which installed boilers are due for service?

After startup each boiler stays in the system as the equipment its service calls and contracts attach to. A service call carries a priority and a response time, and its resolved and closed times are stamped by the system, so response times can't be edited after the fact. Renewing a service contract creates a new contract linked to the old one, so the history of what was covered survives.

## What should a boiler or vessel shop ask before choosing software?

1. **Does it keep the heat number on every piece cut from a plate**, or only on the plate you received?
2. **Can it print the data report package from shop records**, or does someone assemble it in Word at the end?
3. **Does it track welder continuity** per process, so a lapsed welder is caught before the weld, not at the audit?
4. **Does it work beside QuickBooks Online**, sending invoices and bills without double entry, or does it ask you to replace your books?
5. **Does job costing use real purchase orders and logged hours**, or estimates someone types in?

## Where can I read up on the ASME rules behind these records?

In our [ASME guides](/asme), each written to the 2025 Edition from ASME's and the National Board's own pages. The
ones Code shops ask about most: [Section VIII Division 1 vs 2](/asme/section-viii) and
[Section I vs Section IV](/asme/section-i-vs-iv) for which book a job is built to; [Section IX](/asme/section-ix) for
welding qualification; [ASME stamps](/asme/stamps) and [Section XIII relief devices](/asme/section-xiii) for the
certificates; [which ASME edition each state requires](/asme/state-boiler-laws) and [how Code editions work](/asme/editions);
[B31.1 vs B31.3](/asme/b31-1-vs-b31-3) for piping; and [buying ASME equipment from India](/asme/buying-from-india).

## Boundary

The system was first built for a boiler and pressure vessel manufacturer in India and runs that business every day; this North American version is the same code with ASME records, US units, sales tax, an estimate of US payroll withholding and QuickBooks Online, shown here on a sample company. It has not yet been used by a US or Canadian shop. QuickBooks sending covers invoices, payments, vendor bills and bill payments; credit and debit notes are not sent yet, and a document edited after it was sent is not sent again. The system records the shop's code work; it does not replace the shop's [quality control manual](/asme/quality-control-manual) or the Authorized Inspector.

body:
## Can I try it before talking to anyone?

Yes. A live demo runs at [construction-erp.ahromlabs.com](https://construction-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo) with a made-up contractor, Northstone Infra of Ahmedabad, which does waterproofing and repair work and trades construction chemicals. It has four sites with about two and a half months of history: a basement waterproofing job at Mehta Delta Towers, a hotel terrace, a podium slab repair with column jacketing, and a club's pool epoxy lining, one of them losing money. Leave your name and email, pick a login (director, project manager, site engineer, storekeeper or accountant) and use the real screens; each login sees what that role works with. The data resets every night, so nothing you do reaches anyone.

## What does a contractor need that Tally or a spreadsheet doesn't give?

Work measured against the BOQ, cost per site and bills built from the measurements. Tally keeps the books well, but it doesn't know which BOQ line was done today, what material went into which site, or whether a site is spending more than its estimate. A contractor's records start on site, so the system starts there: daily reports, attendance and material used, which then feed the RA bills, the site's cost and the accounts.

## Can site engineers report from the phone?

Yes: one daily report per site per day, built for a phone. The engineer marks attendance first (present, half day or absent, one tap per worker), then fills the report: quantity done against each BOQ line, labour by trade (filled from attendance), material used from the site's own stock, weather, issues and up to six photos. The project manager approves it or sends it back with a note, and only approved work counts toward the site's progress. See [daily progress reports](/construction/daily-progress-reports) for what a report should record and the site records CPWD works keep.

## How are RA bills made?

From measurements against the contract BOQ, never typed totals. A site's BOQ is copied from the client's accepted quotation; once work is reported against a line, only its quantity can change, so past bills keep their meaning. Measurements are recorded against the BOQ or filled from approved work, and the next [RA bill](/construction/ra-bills) takes everything not yet billed: previous, this bill and up-to-date quantities and amounts per line, CGST and SGST or IGST by place of supply, and the amount in words, as a PDF. Bills move from draft to submitted, certified and paid, and paid goes into the cash book. Quantities measured beyond the BOQ are flagged for the client's approval. See [the measurement book](/construction/measurement-book) for the record behind the bill.

## Is each site making money?

The director dashboard shows it per site: contract value, value of approved work, billed, cost to date and margin. Cost to date is material used on site, labour from attendance and wages, site cash spent and machine days. Against the value of approved work it gives the margin so far; scaled to the whole contract, it projects where the site will finish against its estimate. Sites are marked on track, over budget or losing money, next to what needs attention today: reports waiting for approval, sites low on cash, materials below minimum. See [job cost and margin per site](/construction/job-cost-per-site) for the method.

## How is material controlled across the godown and sites?

Material arrives into the godown from suppliers and is transferred to sites; each site holds its own stock, and material used is taken from it on the daily report. Nothing can be sent or used that isn't there. The daily stock report has the columns of a stores register kept in Excel: opening, receipt, dispatch and closing per material, for one location or all, as CSV or print. Material used is also compared with the BOQ norm, so over-consumption on a site shows up the same week; see [material consumption against BOQ](/construction/material-consumption-vs-boq).

## How is site cash (kharchi) accounted for?

Each site's in-charge holds a cash float and records spends from the phone with a photo of the receipt and, for a GST bill, the shop's GSTIN; anything entered three days late is flagged, and a site can't spend more cash than it holds. Every Thursday the site submits the week's spends as one claim; accounts approve or return it, approved claims go out in a bank upload file, and paying a claim tops the site's cash back up and lands in the finance book.

## How are workers on record and paid?

Each worker's KYC is captured on a phone: Aadhaar (only the last four digits are kept), PAN, bank, UAN and photos of the documents, and the same phone or Aadhaar can't be added twice. The monthly wage register works out days from attendance, PF and ESIC for workers on the company's rolls, TDS for subcontractors past the limits, advances and totals per gang, and each worker is paid once a month. Gate passes need complete KYC, record where the worker stays and print as an ID card. See [daily-wage payroll](/services/daily-wage-payroll).

## Does it work with Tally, GST and TDS?

Tally stays the statutory book; the system keeps project cost. Invoices, RA bills, supplier receipts and repaid site cash download as a Tally import file, with the site as the cost centre. The month's GST checklist shows output tax and the GSTR-1 summary by customer and HSN from the system's own bills, and what's missing (HSN, GSTIN, site bills without the shop's GSTIN). The TDS register lists deductions from subcontractor wages with deposit and return dates. See [GST on works contracts](/construction/gst-on-works-contracts) and [TDS on payments to contractors](/construction/tds-on-contractor-payments).

## What does Datum AI answer?

Datum AI sits in the corner of every screen and answers in plain words, in English or Hinglish, with the same figures the screens show: which sites are over budget, who hasn't sent today's report, how much PU membrane is in the godown, who owes us money past 60 days, whose KYC is pending, which machines are idle. The model only picks which look-up to run; the numbers come from the system's own queries. Site engineers never see money, margins or payroll through it. The demo gives two free questions; see [Datum AI for contractors](/ai-assistant/construction-contractors).

## What else is in it?

A trading desk for construction chemicals (rate card with backup suppliers, quotes with options, a credit gate before dispatch, part deliveries, GST invoices and an e-way bill task for accounts), machinery with QR labels and idle days, receivables ageing with weekly follow-ups and escalation to the director after 30 days, and a weekly progress report for the client built from the approved daily reports.

## What should a contractor ask any software vendor?

1. **Are RA bills built from measurements**, or does someone type the totals?
2. **Does each site's cost come from real material issues, attendance and site cash**, or from estimates?
3. **Does the site engineer's report work on a cheap phone on site**, with photos and attendance?
4. **Can site staff be kept away from company money and margins**, enforced on the server, not just hidden?
5. **Does it hand Tally what accounts needs**, without retyping, and keep project cost apart?

## Boundary

The system was built for a waterproofing and repair contractor that also trades construction chemicals; it is built, not yet live at the client. Everything above is shown on sample data in the demo. It doesn't yet deduct security deposit, TDS, GST TDS or mobilisation and secured advances on RA bills, work out price escalation, or produce a WIP schedule; those are parts we'd build for a contractor who needs them.

na.body:
## Can I try it before talking to anyone?

Yes. A live demo runs at [construction-erp-us.ahromlabs.com](https://construction-erp-us.ahromlabs.com/demo) with a made-up contractor, Northstone Builders of Garland, Texas, a waterproofing and concrete restoration contractor with a supply division. It has four jobs: a garage waterproofing job at Halvorsen Tower with an approved change order, a hotel roof deck, a podium deck repair with column jacketing, and a club pool lining that's finished, one of them losing money. Leave your name and email, pick a login (director, project manager, site engineer, storekeeper or accountant) and use the real screens in dollars, imperial units and US dates. The data resets every night, so nothing you do reaches anyone.

## What does a specialty contractor need that QuickBooks alone doesn't give?

Work measured against the schedule of values, cost per job and pay applications built from that work. QuickBooks keeps the books, but it doesn't know which line of the schedule was done today, what material went to which job, or whether a job is spending more than its estimate. A contractor's records start in the field, so the system starts there: daily reports, attendance and material used, which feed the pay applications, the job's cost and the books.

## Can crews report from the field on a phone?

Yes: one daily report per job per day, built for a phone. Attendance comes first (present, half day or absent, one tap per person), then the report: quantity done against each line of the schedule of values, labor by trade (filled from attendance), material used from the job's own stock, weather, issues and up to six photos. The project manager approves it or sends it back with a note, and only approved work counts toward the job's progress.

## How are pay applications made?

From work measured against the schedule of values. A job's schedule of values is copied from the owner's accepted estimate or entered line by line. Work is measured against each line, or filled from approved daily reports, and stored materials are added per line. The [pay application](/construction/pay-applications) shows scheduled value, previous, this period, stored materials, % complete and balance to finish, holds [retainage](/construction/retainage), works out the current payment due and downloads as a G702/G703-style PDF with the architect's certificate. Line 7, less previous certificates, is recomputed from each earlier application, so certified amounts never drift.

## How are change orders handled?

A change order is raised as its own estimate against the accepted contract estimate; once accepted, its lines join the schedule of values labeled CO 1, CO 2 and are billed apart, so the pay application shows the original contract sum, the net change by change orders and the revised sum. Draft and sent change orders stay pending and are never billed. On the sample tower job, change order 1 adds $6,504 to a $245,856 schedule of values. See [change orders](/construction/change-orders).

## Are lien waivers tracked?

Yes, per pay application: ours to the owner, and each sub's and supplier's for the money they were paid, conditional on progress until paid and then unconditional, with the date each came in. See [lien waivers](/construction/lien-waivers) for the four types and the states with statutory forms.

## Is each job making money?

The director dashboard shows it per job: contract value, value of approved work, billed, cost to date and margin. Cost to date is material used, labor from attendance and pay, site cash spent and equipment days. Against the value of approved work it gives the margin so far; scaled to the whole contract, it projects where the job will finish against its estimate. Jobs are marked on track, over budget or losing money, next to what needs attention today.

## Does it work with QuickBooks Online?

Yes. QuickBooks Online stays the books: issued invoices, pay applications and payments go across with each project as a job under its client, supplier bills for goods received at the yard and the payments against them go too, and every record shows whether it is in QuickBooks. QuickBooks works out the sales tax on supply invoices. In the demo it is connected to an Intuit sandbox company. See [connecting QuickBooks Online to an operations system](/manufacturing/quickbooks-integration).

## How are crews paid?

Each worker's onboarding is captured on a phone: photo, photo ID, I-9, W-4 (or W-9 for a 1099 subcontractor) and direct deposit, with photos of the documents. The monthly pay register works out days from attendance at each person's rate, less advances, with totals per crew, and each worker is paid once a month. Payroll taxes stay with your payroll provider. Gate passes need complete onboarding and print as an ID badge.

## What does Datum AI answer?

Datum AI sits in the corner of every screen and answers with the same figures the screens show: which jobs are over budget, who hasn't sent today's report, what's in the yard, who owes us past 60 days, which equipment is idle. The model only picks which look-up to run; the numbers come from the system's own queries. Field staff never see money, margins or payroll through it. The demo gives two free questions; see [Datum AI for contractors](/ai-assistant/construction-contractors).

## What else is in it?

Yard and job stock with receipts, transfers and a daily stock sheet per location; site cash per job with receipt photos and a weekly claim; equipment with QR labels and idle days; receivables by age with weekly follow-ups and escalation to the director after 30 days; a weekly progress report for the owner built from the approved daily reports; and a supply desk that quotes from a rate card with backup suppliers, holds shipping until terms are met, and invoices with sales tax.

## What should a contractor ask any software vendor?

1. **Are pay applications built from measured work on the schedule of values**, or typed in?
2. **Are change orders kept apart until approved**, and billed as their own lines?
3. **Is retainage held per application, on stored materials too**, and recomputed, not carried by hand?
4. **Does job cost come from real material, labor and site cash**, or from estimates?
5. **Does it work beside QuickBooks Online**, without double entry?

## Boundary

The system was built for a waterproofing and repair contractor in India that also trades construction chemicals; it is built, not yet live at the client. This North American version is the same code with US terms, pay applications, change orders, lien waivers, onboarding and QuickBooks Online, shown here on a sample company, and it has not yet been used by a US or Canadian contractor. It doesn't yet produce a WIP schedule, bill a retainage release, track retainage held from subcontractors or keep a change log with notice dates; those are parts we'd build.

body:
## Can I try it before talking to anyone?

Yes. A live demo of the inventory and CRM side runs at [electronics-erp.ahromlabs.com](https://electronics-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo) with a made-up trader, Acme Components: reels with QR labels in a main store and a partner store, customer purchase orders, dispatches and approvals waiting. Leave a name and email, pick a login (owner, manager, store staff, partner store or customer) and use the real screens. Uploads are switched off there, the assistant Ohm AI takes two questions per visitor, and the data resets every night, so nothing you do reaches anyone.

## Why does an import-trading business end up typing the same invoice twice?

Because operations and accounts live in different places. Purchase orders, supplier invoices, freight bills and customs paperwork arrive as PDFs; the team reads them, works in spreadsheets or a web app, and then someone types the same figures into TallyPrime. [LS Technologies](/work#ls-technologies), an electronics-components import and export business, had exactly that shape. The system Ahrom Labs built reads the documents, keeps the operational record, and posts the accounting entry into Tally itself.

## Can a cloud app post directly into TallyPrime?

Not directly — TallyPrime's integration gateway only listens on the machine that runs Tally. A small agent on that PC bridges the two: it picks up approved invoices every 30 seconds and posts them as vouchers, syncs voucher status and outstanding bills back every 15 minutes, and refreshes ledgers, stock items and voucher types nightly. A ledger that doesn't exist yet in Tally is flagged for a person, never created by the software. See [Posting vouchers into TallyPrime from a cloud app](/notes/tally-voucher-posting); the protocol code is open-sourced as [tally-voucher-xml](https://github.com/Ahrom-Labs/tally-voucher-xml). The agent is one of four ways Ahrom Labs connects to Tally — alongside an MCP server and a CSV or JSON file route — compared in [Four ways to connect a business system to TallyPrime](/notes/connecting-tallyprime-four-ways).

## How accurate is AI extraction on import documents?

Measured on real usage, the share of documents needing no correction is 95% for purchase orders, 94% for purchase invoices, 91% for freight invoices, 89% for bank statements and 88% for bills of entry. Those are lower than the 95–99% many invoice-automation tools advertise — but a 2026 benchmark review found those claims are measured under vendor-chosen conditions, with no independent benchmark ([Parseur](https://parseur.com/blog/ai-invoice-processing-benchmarks)). These are per-document-type numbers from a live system, and every document still waits for a person's approval before anything reaches the books. See [AI extraction with a human in the loop](/notes/ai-extraction-human-in-the-loop).

## What happens when Tally rejects a voucher?

The failure is classified before anything else happens. If Tally is simply offline, the voucher stays queued and posts on the next 30-second cycle, with no restart. If Tally rejects it — a missing ledger, a duplicate — it's held with the exact reason attached until a person fixes it. After every sync, the system checks what Tally actually holds; a voucher deleted inside Tally is marked unconfirmed again.

## How are import duty, IGST and clearing charges booked?

Each line of a bill of entry — basic customs duty, IGST paid on import, freight and insurance — is extracted as its own line and posted to its own ledger, so IGST paid at customs never mixes with IGST on domestic purchases. Clearing and forwarding charges are routed to named ledgers by what they are — CFS, delivery order, handling, THS, IGM, agency, warehousing and more — and anything the rules don't recognise goes to a miscellaneous ledger rather than being guessed. A freight bill books to a single freight purchase ledger with its GST. The document type itself is decided from structure: a purchase order has no invoice number or e-invoice reference, an e-invoice has an IRN, a freight bill carries airway-bill and airport details. An extracted purchase order becomes a purchase-order record rather than an accounting entry.

## How is every reel labelled and found again?

Stock is modelled the way a component store holds it: items, reels, and boxes of reels. Receiving an item creates its reels at the item's standard pack quantity and spreads them across boxes, each reel and box with its own number and a printed QR label — reel labels carry the item, quantity and batch; box labels list the reels inside. Reel and box numbers re-derive their counter from the data before each allocation, so a manual edit can never cause two reels to share a number.

Finding a reel later is one search box across reel number, item, box, customer and invoice, with each reel's full dispatch history, and the result exports to CSV exactly as filtered on screen.

## Can a shipment be checked against the customer's purchase order before it leaves?

Yes — that is how dispatch works. Reels are scanned into a shipment with a phone camera or a scanner; scanning a box adds only the reels in it that can actually ship and lists the rest with the reason, and scanning a reel twice is refused with an error sound. A reel ships whole or in part: a partial dispatch reduces the reel's quantity and leaves it in stock.

When the customer's purchase order is picked, the shipment is compared with it line by line — an item missing, short, over, or not on the order at all — and it can't be submitted until the two agree. The packing list is generated from the same shipment, grouped by item with each item's standard pack quantity, and can be reprinted later by customer and invoice.

## How is stock kept straight across two stores?

Every reel belongs to a store, and stock moves between stores by transfer — a single reel, or a whole box. A whole-box transfer moves every reel in it or none of them. A reel can also move on its own, so reels from one box can legitimately sit in two stores; each reel's move is logged separately, so undoing a transfer reverts exactly that reel and nothing else. Two people moving the same reel at the same moment can't both succeed — verified by forcing exactly that race.

Staff at the second store are locked to it on the server, and each day their manager signs off the previous day's dispatch summary before anyone there can record new movements. A dispatch always records the store the reel is actually in, never the store picked on screen — a rule added after a mislabelled dispatch showed that the two could disagree.

## Who approves stock movements?

Staff record receipts, dispatches and transfers; managers' actions go through immediately, and staff actions wait for approval. A manager can approve, reject with a reason, or correct and approve in one step. The queued request is replayed through exactly the same code path as an immediate one, so an approved action can't behave differently from a direct one.

## What can the owner see?

- **Stock summary** per item, as of today or any past date, per store or across both.
- **Analytics** — monthly receipts and dispatches, ageing of stock in hand and of dispatched reels, item velocity, top customers and an inventory timeline.
- **Dead and low stock** — an item only appears for a store when it has live stock there, so an empty store doesn't flag the whole catalogue as low.
- **Daily report**, on screen and as a PDF — the day's receipts and dispatches by item, transfers, dead and low stock, and pending approvals.

A customer can be given a read-only stock view. That account is limited at the server to the stock summary: every other endpoint in the system — about 60 — was tested against it and refused.

## What should a component trader ask before choosing inventory software?

1. **Does it track reels, or only item totals?** Partial reels, boxes and labels are where component stock actually goes wrong.
2. **Is dispatch checked against the customer's purchase order** before the shipment leaves, not after the complaint?
3. **What happens to import paperwork?** Bills of entry, freight and clearing bills should reach the books without being typed twice — and with duty and import IGST on the right ledgers.
4. **How does it work with Tally?** Replace it, sync with it, or post into it — and what happens when Tally rejects an entry.
5. **Who can see and change what?** Staff, managers, a second store, a customer — each enforced by the server, not just hidden on screen.

## Boundary

The Tally link depends on the office PC running Tally being switched on; if it's off, nothing posts until it's back, and the queue resumes on its own. This is not a cloud-to-cloud integration, because Tally doesn't offer one.

The inventory identifies an item by its code and description; manufacturer part numbers, alternates and date codes aren't separate fields, and a batch is a free-text label printed on the reel. Moisture-sensitivity (MSL) floor life isn't tracked, and stock is located by store, not by bin. Customs duty and freight are booked to their own ledgers rather than spread into each item's landed cost.

na.body:
## Can I try it before talking to anyone?

Yes. A live demo runs at [electronics-erp-us.ahromlabs.com](https://electronics-erp-us.ahromlabs.com/demo) with a
made-up distributor, Acme Components, its Main Store and a Partner Store, customers such as Brightline Appliances and
Voltix Motors, and about four months of history: purchase orders complete, part-shipped and in procurement, requests
waiting for approval, and invoices in QuickBooks. Leave a name and email, pick one of six logins (owner, manager, store
staff, partner store manager or worker, or the customer portal) and use the real screens in dollars and US dates.
Uploads and settings changes are switched off, the assistant Ohm AI takes two questions per visitor, and the data
resets every night.

## Why track reels instead of quantities?

Because customers order pieces and stores ship reels. Knowing each reel tells you which ones fill an order and what is
left on a part-used one. Receiving an item creates its reels at the item's standard pack quantity (2,500 for an
LM358DR op-amp in the demo) and spreads them across boxes; a reel ships whole or in part, and a part shipment reduces
that reel's quantity and leaves it in stock.

## How is every reel labelled and found again?

With a QR label on every reel and every box, printed when the stock is received: reel labels carry the item, quantity
and batch, box labels list the reels inside. One search box finds a reel by its number, item, box, customer or
invoice, with its dispatch history, and exports to CSV exactly as filtered. Reel and box numbers are rechecked against
the data before each one is issued, so a manual edit can't make two reels share a number.

## Can a shipment be checked against the customer's PO before it leaves?

Yes: it can't be submitted until the two agree. Reels are scanned into a shipment with a phone camera or a scanner;
scanning a box adds only the reels in it that can ship and lists the rest with the reason, and a reel scanned twice
is refused. Once the customer's PO is picked, the shipment is compared with it line by line (an item missing, short,
over, or not on the order), and the packing list is printed from the same shipment.

## How is stock reserved for a customer's order?

Whole reels in the main store are set aside for each PO line, oldest stock first, until the line is covered. A
reserved reel scanned for a different order shows "Reserved · PO …", and shipping it needs a manager's override. A
worked example with made-up quantities: a PO line for 12,000 LM358DR reserves five reels of 2,500 (12,500, so the last
reel overshoots). The shipment takes four full reels and 2,000 pieces from the fifth, which stays in stock with 500.

## What happens when stock is short?

The shortfall goes on a list for purchasing. What open PO lines still need is pooled by item under "To procure";
staff pick items into a draft procurement order and track it through its stages. When the reels arrive and are
received against that order, they are reserved to the waiting PO lines first, earliest dispatch date first, and the
order closes when everything has arrived.

## How is stock kept straight across two stores or a partner warehouse?

Every reel belongs to a store, and stock moves between stores only by transfer: one reel, or a whole box (all its
reels or none). Partner store staff are locked to their store on the server, and each day their manager signs off the
previous day's dispatches before anyone there can record new movements. A dispatch always records the store the reel
is actually in, not the one picked on screen.

## Who approves stock movements?

A manager. Store staff record receipts, dispatches and transfers, and those wait for approval; a manager can approve,
reject with a reason, or correct and approve in one step, and managers' own entries go through at once. An approved
request runs through exactly the same code as a direct entry, so it can't behave differently.

## Can customers see their own orders?

Yes, in a read-only portal. The customer login in the demo (Brightline) sees its own purchase orders, each line's
status (reserved, in procurement, shipped) and a progress bar, plus a stock view; it sees no other customer, no
supplier and no cost.

## Does it work with QuickBooks Online?

Yes, in the demo against an Intuit sandbox company. The owner connects QuickBooks once and maps seven accounts (bank,
receivables, payables, sales, inventory, purchases, freight). Sales invoices go to QuickBooks with their customer,
each line marked taxable or not, and QuickBooks' automated sales tax works the tax out; receipts, approved vendor
bills and bill payments go too. Each row shows whether it is in QuickBooks, failed with a Retry, or not sent. Credit
notes aren't sent yet, and an invoice edited after sending isn't sent again. More in
[connecting QuickBooks Online to a shop system](/manufacturing/quickbooks-integration).

## What should a component distributor ask before choosing inventory software?

1. **Does it track reels, or only item totals?** Part reels, boxes and labels are where component stock goes wrong.
2. **Is a shipment checked against the customer's PO before it leaves**, not after the complaint?
3. **Can stock be reserved for a customer's order**, so two orders can't count on the same reels?
4. **How does it work with QuickBooks**, and what happens when a post fails?
5. **Who can see and change what?** Staff, managers, a partner store, a customer, each enforced by the server, not
   just hidden on screen.

For counting, lots and FIFO in a warehouse, see [inventory control for distributors](/manufacturing/distributor-inventory-control).

## Boundary

The system was built for an electronic components importer in India and runs that business every day; this North
American version is the same code with dollars, US dates and QuickBooks Online, shown on a sample company. It has not
yet been used by a US or Canadian distributor. Stock is located by store, not by bin; manufacturer part numbers, date
codes and moisture-sensitivity floor life aren't separate fields, and a batch is a free-text label. Sales tax is one
rate per line, worked out by QuickBooks when connected; the system doesn't hold customers' resale certificates or
report sales by state (see [resale certificates](/sales-tax/resale-certificates)), and we'd build those for a
distributor that needs them. The figure of 5,256 reels is the client's in India.

body:
## Can I try it before talking to anyone?

Yes. A live demo runs at [interiors-erp.ahromlabs.com](https://interiors-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo) with two made-up sister companies, Acme Interiors and Acme Furniture: projects on site with milestones and site visits, workshop orders with three weeks of worksheet history, vendor POs with deliveries, freight checked against a rate card, GST invoices and a shared cash book. Leave a name and email, pick a login (owner, manager or office staff) and use the real screens. File uploads are switched off there, and the data resets every night, so nothing you do reaches anyone.

## Why do design firms outgrow spreadsheets and chat?

A design-and-build job touches clients, site visits, vendors, labour, freight and payments at once, usually spread across a spreadsheet per project and a chat group per site. The owners know how it all connects; nobody else does. [Savistar and Saag](/work#savistar-saag) — an interior design firm and a furniture workshop under the same owners — moved all of it into one system: workers, clients, vendors and freight, projects and site visits on the design side, workshop orders on the furniture side.

## Can a design studio and its furniture workshop share one system?

Yes, and without the weight of a multi-company ERP. Both businesses share one client list and one combined ledger; a design job lives under Projects and a furniture order under Orders, and each invoice carries its own company's letterhead, logo and GSTIN when the PDF is generated. It's a single app modeling two business lines — a sister-concern arrangement, in Indian accounting terms — which is exactly as much structure as the business needs. See [Two companies, one book](/notes/two-companies-one-book).

## How is a design project tracked from brief to handover?

Each project has a checklist of milestones with due dates, a log of site visits — who went, when, and what they found — and the workshop orders and vendor purchase orders that belong to it, on one page. Every conversation with a client is logged against the client and, when it's about a specific job, pinned to that project, so the history of a decision isn't buried in someone's chat.

The home screen is a month calendar of what's due across both businesses: tasks, project milestones, site visits and workshop delivery dates, with the weather forecast alongside for planning site work, and today's and overdue tasks beside it. Owners assign tasks to anyone; staff see their own and can only create tasks for themselves.

## Can a quotation start from a BOQ?

Yes, since October 2026. Each studio keeps its own BOQ library, started from our [interior BOQ item library](/boq/items) and reworded to its own wording. A quotation is built room by room from it, with quantities worked out from site dimensions and each line checked for a missing board grade, thickness, finish or [measurement basis](/boq/measurement-rules). Payment stages printed on the quote become draft invoices once the client accepts. It hasn't been used on a real project yet; the free [BOQ checker](/boq/check) shows the same checks without an account.

## How does the workshop know who made what?

A workshop order can come from a design project or straight from a walk-in client, and moves from pending to in progress, done and delivered. The daily worksheet records each worker's attendance — present, half day or absent, with in and out times — and what they worked on: which order, which part, from when to when, with a rating. Each order's work history then shows who worked on which part, and when.

## How are daily-wage and salaried workers paid?

Each worker is paid either a monthly salary or a daily wage. Advances and expenses are recorded as they happen, and the month's payroll is computed rather than worked out on paper: a daily-wage worker's days present — a half day counting as half — times their rate, or a salaried worker's monthly salary, minus that month's advances. Each payout is recorded for its period with the gross, the deductions and the net, so the figure paid and how it was reached stay together.

## How do you stop staff seeing the whole cash book?

By filtering at the point the data is fetched, not by hiding buttons. Staff log day-to-day cash, but their view of the cash ledger contains only the entries they created. Bank data isn't scoped for staff at all — every request for it from a staff account is refused before any query runs. Owners see everything.

## How are vendor and freight overcharges caught?

Every incoming charge is compared against a known reference rate, and anything that deviates is flagged automatically — instead of trusting every bill or asking someone to audit each line by hand. For freight, the reference is a rate card per transporter and per route — from one location to another, the amount expected — so a trip billed above its route's rate is flagged the moment it's entered, and each vendor shows its count of overcharges. It catches overcharges as long as the reference rates are kept current.

## How are partial deliveries and advances tracked?

A material order placed with a vendor is linked to the project or workshop order it's for, and every delivery and return against it is recorded as it happens. The order shows as open, complete, partially returned or fully returned, and what's still to arrive is computed from those deliveries.

Outstanding amounts — a partial delivery, an advance against pay — are computed from the underlying transactions every time they're shown, rather than kept as a running total that can drift from the records that produced it.

## Can bank statements and bills come in without retyping?

A bank statement is uploaded as a PDF, its transactions are read by AI, and an owner or manager reviews them line by line, adding a note or attaching the receipt behind any entry. Cash entries carry their attachments too. Invoices are raised per client, optionally against a project, with HSN codes and a GST rate per line; the CGST and SGST totals are computed from the lines every time rather than stored, and each invoice moves from draft to sent to paid.

Nothing is ever hard-deleted: a removed record stops showing but stays in the database, and deleting at all needs an owner, admin or manager.

## What should a design studio ask before choosing software?

1. **Does it hold the design side and the workshop side together** — projects, site visits, workshop orders and vendors — or only one of them?
2. **Can it pay daily-wage workers** from real attendance, with advances deducted, not from a separate notebook?
3. **Does it check vendor and freight bills** against what they should cost, or just record them?
4. **If you run two companies, does each invoice carry the right company's name and GSTIN** from one system?
5. **Who can see the money?** Staff logging petty cash shouldn't see the bank account — enforced by the server, not by hiding a menu.

## What did the owners say?

> "They really took the time to understand our concerns and requirements, and the system was built the way we had envisioned it. It has brought much more structure, visibility, and control to the way we operate."
>
> — Sachi & Haripriya, owners of Savistar and Saag

## Boundary

This is one shared app for two related businesses, not a multi-tenant platform: adding an unrelated third company would mean a different design, not a new setting.

Quotations were added in October 2026 and haven't been used on a real project yet: the studio's own BOQ library (started from our [interior BOQ item library](/boq/items)), quantities from site dimensions, and payment stages that become draft invoices once a quote is accepted. Quotes and invoices charge CGST and SGST, or IGST when the site is in another state. There is no 3D design or mood boards, and no client portal — clients are served by the team, not by a login. The free [interior BOQ checker](/boq/check) on this site runs the same line checks without an account.

body:
## When did IBR 2026 replace IBR 1950?

The Indian Boiler Regulations, 2026 replaced the Indian Boiler Regulations, 1950 on 1 October 2026, the day they were published in the Gazette of India (Extraordinary, No. 596). The Central Boilers Board made them under section 40 of the Boilers Act, 2025, which itself repealed the Boilers Act, 1923.

The supersession is "except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession", so what was done under IBR 1950 before 1 October 2026 is not undone by the change.

## Were the IBR forms renumbered?

Yes. The IBR 2026 forms run from Form I to Form XXIII, and most folder documents changed number. The maker's certificate of manufacture and test, Form III under IBR 1950, is now Form IV Part A. The Inspecting Authority's certificate, Form II(1) or II(2), is now Form I Part B or Part C. The steel maker's certificate, Form IV, is now Form V Part A.

Every form, with its old name, is on [the IBR 2026 forms list](/ibr/forms).

## Can IBR certificates be filed electronically now?

Yes. Under regulation 8 of IBR 2026, the certificates, drawings and specifications that go with a boiler's registration application may be submitted electronically with digital signatures. Well-known pipe and tube makers may also issue their certificates (Form IV Part B and Part C) online with a digital signature.

## How long must boiler records be kept under IBR 2026?

Regulation 308 sets three periods. The Inspecting Authority keeps a boiler's certificates and approved drawings for at least three years after registration. The owner keeps them for the entire life of the boiler, and hands them to any new owner. The manufacturer keeps them, including Form V Part B, for at least five years. See [boiler record keeping under IBR 2026](/ibr/record-keeping).

## What changed for boiler manufacturers?

A firm seeking recognition as a manufacturer applies to an Inspecting Authority in its own state with the manufacturer questionnaire, Form III, which is new in IBR 2026 (regulation 7(1)(b)(v)). Recognition lasts three years, and renewal is applied for at least ninety days before it expires (regulation 7(4)). Components can be erected at site on the strength of a final inspection report in Form VIII approved by the Competent Person (regulation 293(2)). The steel maker's certificate, now Form V Part A, gives ultimate tensile strength in kilograms per square millimetre; the IBR 1950 Form IV gave it in tons.

## What changed in registration?

Under regulation 300 of IBR 2026, the Inspector inspects the boiler, conducts the hydraulic test and issues a provisional order in Form X, under section 14 of the Boilers Act, 2025; under IBR 1950 the provisional order was Form V. The boiler's record is the Memorandum of Inspection Book, now Form XI. See [documents for boiler registration](/ibr/registration-documents).

A Memorandum of Inspection Book shall be prepared for each boiler in Form-XI
The Memorandum of Inspection Book shall be kept clean and up-to-date

On transfer of a boiler from one state to another, the memorandum of inspection book and the registration book shall, on the request of Chief Inspector of the state to which the boiler has been transferred, be forwarded to that officer

body:
## How long must a boiler manufacturer keep IBR records?

A boiler manufacturer keeps the boiler's records for at least five years under regulation 308(4) of IBR 2026. The same rule covers makers of economisers and steam pipes. The records are the Inspecting Authority's certificates (Form I Part B or C), the component certificates (Form IV Parts B, C and D), the material certificates (Form V Parts A and B), the economiser certificates (Forms XV and XVI) and copies of the approved drawings.

## How long must the boiler owner keep them?

The owner keeps the boiler's certificates and approved drawings for the entire life of the boiler under regulation 308(2). If the boiler is sold, the records go to the new owner, who keeps them on the same terms (regulation 308(3)).

## How long does the Inspecting Authority keep them?

The Inspecting Authority keeps a boiler's records, including Form IV Part A, for at least three years after registration, and may then send them to the owner (regulation 308(1)).

## Where is the boiler's inspection book kept?

The Memorandum of Inspection Book, [Form XI](/ibr/forms/form-xi), is kept in the Chief Inspector's office except when the Competent Person needs it for an inspection (regulation 306). The Chief Inspector also keeps a registration book with the same particulars (regulation 307). If a boiler moves to another state, both books go to that state's Chief Inspector on request (regulation 309).

## When can the original certificates be asked for?

Within three years of a boiler's registration, if a question arises about its fitness for the approved working pressure, the Chief Inspector can ask the owner to obtain and furnish the original documents (regulation 8(d)(ii)).

## Why does five years matter for a manufacturer?

Five years of certificates for every boiler made is a large archive. In one boiler manufacturer's sample, each [material test certificate](/systems/material-test-certificate) was used across about 3.2 boilers, so one certificate is evidence in several folders. The system Ahrom Labs built for that manufacturer keeps them in one bank indexed by certificate, cast and plate number, rather than copied into each folder. See [how that system keeps test certificates](/notes/ibr-statutory-folder-from-bom).

body:
## Which documents go with a boiler registration application?

Regulation 8 of the Indian Boiler Regulations, 2026 lists what goes to the Chief Inspector with an application to register a boiler. They may be filed on paper or electronically with digital signatures.

1. **The Inspecting Authority's certificate:** [Form I Part B](/ibr/forms/form-i-part-b) for a shop-assembled boiler, or [Form I Part C](/ibr/forms/form-i-part-c) for one assembled at site. [Form I Part D](/ibr/forms/form-i-part-d) replaces either when permitted variations apply.
2. **The maker's certificate of manufacture and test:** [Form IV Part A](/ibr/forms/form-iv-part-a), signed by the maker.
3. **Drawings:** for a shop-assembled boiler, drawings showing principal dimensions, sections, maker's number, stamp position, bill of material, welding details and design parameters.
4. **Material certificates:** the steel maker's [Form V Part A](/ibr/forms/form-v-part-a), and the [Form V Part B](/ibr/forms/form-v-part-b) extract of every [material test certificate](/systems/material-test-certificate) used.

## What else is needed for some boilers?

Fusion-welded drums need a diagram of weld repairs and the heat-treatment temperature charts (regulation 8(d)(v)). Alloy steels used in the creep range in the furnace or superheater zone need two 1,000-hour stress rupture tests for each grade (regulation 8(d)(vi)). Boilers under 20 tons per hour carry all their mountings and fittings certificates; at 20 tons per hour and above, mountings for site-assembled boilers may be supplied separately (regulation 8(d)(vii)).

## What happens after the application is filed?

Under regulation 300, the Inspector inspects the boiler at site for transit damage and checks the maker's certificate against the boiler. The Inspector then conducts the hydraulic test and issues a provisional order in [Form X](/ibr/forms/form-x), so the boiler can be used while registration completes. The particulars and test results go into the Memorandum of Inspection Book, [Form XI](/ibr/forms/form-xi), which goes to the Chief Inspector with the maker's papers. Once the registry number is issued, the Inspector conducts a steam test and enters it in Form XI (regulation 300(4)); the certificate for use, [Form XII](/ibr/forms/form-xii), follows (regulation 310).

## When is the registry number engraved?

Within one month of receiving it, the registry number is cut into the boiler's front plate or wherever the Inspector points out, and the engraving is reported to the Chief Inspector within the same month (regulation 301). The number sits below the state's letters, for example GT for Gujarat and MR for Maharashtra; a small industrial boiler's number carries an "S" prefix.

A boiler designed to the ASME Code still goes through IBR registration in India. Where IBR 2026 accepts ASME designs, materials and inspection, and how the ASME paperwork lines up with these forms, is in [ASME vs IBR 2026](/asme/asme-vs-ibr) and [ASME data reports](/asme/data-reports).

title: Small industrial boilers under IBR 2026
answer: Under IBR 2026 a small industrial boiler is a shell boiler up to 7 kg/cm² (g) holding more than 25 and up to 500 litres, or a coil, once-through or water tube boiler up to 12 kg/cm² (g) and 150 litres. Its certificate of manufacture and test is Form XXII, which was Form XVII under IBR 1950.
