body:
## What counts as a small industrial boiler under IBR 2026?

A small industrial boiler, under regulation 546 of IBR 2026, is one of two kinds. A shell type boiler working up to 7 kg/cm² (g), with a volumetric capacity of more than 25 litres and up to 500 litres, measured from the feed check valve to the main steam stop valve. Or a coil type, once-through or water tube boiler working up to 12 kg/cm² (g), with a capacity of up to 150 litres. A boiler combining both kinds is held to 7 kg/cm² (g) and 500 litres in total.

## Which stages are inspected for a small shell boiler?

An Inspecting Authority inspects a small industrial boiler during construction (regulation 550). For a shell type boiler, regulation 551 sets four stages: material identification and inspection; each component after welding and drilling; assembly of the boiler; and the hydraulic test. A welded boiler is tested at twice its design pressure, and the maker provides a test coupon for root and face bend tests.

## Which certificate does a small industrial boiler need?

A small industrial boiler's certificate of manufacture and test is [Form XXII](/ibr/forms/form-xxii) (regulation 555(2)). Under IBR 1950 this was Form XVII, which also covered small solar boilers; they now have their own Form XXIII. If the boiler's plate is too small to stamp every detail, the certificate carries them, but the name, works number and year of make are always stamped or shown on the boiler (regulation 553(2)).

## Which plates can a small industrial boiler use, and is a steel maker's certificate needed?

A small industrial boiler's plates are IS 2062 fully killed steel or equivalent, at least 6 mm thick for the shell and heads, and at least 8 mm where heads serve as tube sheets for rolled-in tubes (regulation 548(2)(a)). The steel maker's certificate in Form V Part A is not required for IS 2062 plates, provided every other certification requirement is met (regulation 548(2)(b)).

## How is a small industrial boiler's registry number marked?

A small industrial boiler's registry number carries an "S" prefix below the state's letters, for example "GT" over "S-" and the number for a boiler registered in Gujarat (regulation 301(1)(c)).

title: How to make an interior BOQ, step by step
answer: Make an interior BOQ in 7 steps: read the drawings and finish schedule, split the work room by room and trade, pick each item and its unit, measure and state how, name the material, size, finish and hardware, list exclusions, then price it. A line two contractors would read differently is the line that causes the dispute.
description: Making an interior BOQ from drawings in 7 steps, with the units, specifications and exclusions each line needs, and a sample.

image.alt: A floor plan with an architect's scale ruler resting on it and one room traced over in pencil.

sources.title: IS 1200, Method of measurement of building and civil engineering works (all parts)

body:
## What do you start an interior BOQ from?

A [BOQ](/systems/bill-of-quantities) is only as complete as the drawings behind it: plans, ceiling plans, elevations of every joinery unit, the electrical layout and a finish schedule naming each material. Anything not drawn is either missing from the BOQ or priced as a guess.

## How should the BOQ be split?

By room, then by trade. Group lines room by room (kitchen, master bedroom, bathroom 1) and within each room by trade: civil, false ceiling, flooring, carpentry, painting, electrical, plumbing. The client reads it by room; contractors price it by trade; a site supervisor checks it against both.

## Which unit does each item take?

Use the unit the trade prices in: sq ft for ceilings, floors, panelling and wardrobes; running ft for kitchen cabinets, skirting and coves; number for doors, fittings and drawers; point for wiring. A wardrobe in running ft and another in sq ft can't be compared. The [item library](/boq/items) gives the usual unit for 41 items.

## How is each item measured?

By a stated method, so two contractors count the same thing. For civil-type work, IS 1200 sets the method ([measurement rules](/boq/measurement-rules) has each part's rules): Part 10 for ceilings and linings, Part 11 for floor finishes, dado and skirting, Part 13 for painting building surfaces, Part 21 for woodwork, which is measured net as fixed with nothing added for shape or joints. Modular work has no such standard, so the line must say it: "measured by front elevation, loft excluded".

## What should each line say it is made of?

Every joinery line names the board and its grade (for example IS 303 BWP plywood), the thickness, the finish inside and out, the edge band and the hardware make. Leave one out and the cheapest version of it is what gets priced. See [material specifications](/boq/material-specifications).

## What should the BOQ exclude?

Countertops, appliances, light fittings, sanitaryware and loose furniture are often bought by the client or priced separately. Write them down as excluded or as their own lines; an unlisted exclusion becomes an argument at the final bill.

## When are rates and GST added?

Rates come last: from your own rate analysis or from contractors pricing the same lines. GST is added at the quotation, not in the rates. Changes after this point are [variations](/boq/variation-orders), priced as new lines rather than by editing old ones.

## What does a finished BOQ look like?

Like this extract, with its unit and quantity on every line:

| No | Description | Unit | Qty |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Kitchen base cabinets in 18 mm IS 303 BWP plywood carcass, acrylic shutters, 2 mm PVC edge band, soft-close hinges and channels of [make]; measured by running length, excluding countertop | running ft | 14 |
| 2 | Kitchen wall cabinets 700 mm high in 18 mm IS 303 BWP plywood, laminate shutters, 2 mm PVC edge band, [make] hinges; measured by running length | running ft | 12 |
| 3 | 20 mm granite countertop 625 mm deep, edge moulded, including sink and hob cut-outs | running ft | 14 |
| 4 | Hinged wardrobe in 18 mm IS 303 BWP plywood, 1 mm laminate outside, 0.8 mm inside, 2 mm PVC edge band, [make] soft-close hinges; measured by front elevation, excluding loft | sq ft | 64 |
| 5 | Gypsum board false ceiling 12.5 mm on GI framing, joints taped; measured by plan area of the flat field, excluding coves | sq ft | 180 |

Paste your own into the [checker](/boq/check) to see what each line leaves open, or start from the [Excel template](/boq/template).

## What does this guide not settle?

Quantities, rates and your contract's GST treatment. The steps and units are common practice for interior work in India; IS 1200 governs only the trades it covers. Quantities, rates and the GST treatment of your contract are yours, and your CA's, to settle.

title: Board standards for an interior BOQ: IS 303, IS 710 and others
metaTitle: Board standards for an interior BOQ: IS 303, IS 710
answer: An interior BOQ names the board by its Indian Standard and grade, because "plywood" alone can be priced as the cheapest sheet in the market. IS 303 covers general-purpose plywood (MR, and BWR, renamed BWP by amendment), IS 710 marine plywood, IS 1659 block boards, and IS 3087 and IS 12823 particle boards.
description: The Indian Standards for plywood, block board and particle board, and how to write a joinery BOQ line that can't be substituted.

image.alt: A stack of five board offcuts cut to show their edges: layered plywood, block board with a core of timber strips, particle board, a plain board, and particle board with a thin dark top sheet.

sources.title: IS 303:1989, Plywood for general purposes (third revision), public copy
sources.publisher: Bureau of Indian Standards, via Public.Resource.Org

body:
## Why put the Indian Standard in a BOQ line?

"18 mm plywood with laminate" describes sheets that differ several times over in price and in how they survive a wet kitchen. Naming the standard and grade fixes what is being priced and gives the site something to check: the grade is marked on each sheet.

## What are IS 303 and IS 710 plywood?

IS 303 is plywood for general purposes and IS 710 is marine plywood:

- **IS 303, plywood for general purposes.** The 1989 edition grades plywood by the bond of its adhesive: MR (moisture resistant) and BWR (boiling water resistant), and an amendment renamed BWR as BWP. It also names faces by quality: AA, AB and BB. IS 303:2024 is the current edition in the BIS catalogue; check its grade names when you specify.
- **IS 710, marine plywood**, for wet areas such as vanities and sink bases, where a BOQ wants more than BWP.

## Which standards cover block board and particle board?

IS 1659 for block boards, and IS 3087 and IS 12823 for particle boards:

- **IS 1659, block boards**: a core of timber strips between veneers, used for long shelves and doors.
- **IS 3087**: medium-density particle boards for general purposes.
- **IS 12823**: prelaminated particle boards, the factory-laminated board of most low-cost modular units.
- **IS 2202 (Part 1)**: wooden flush door shutters, solid core, with plywood face panels.

Boards sold under trade names (HDHMR, for example) should be named by product and maker in the line, with the maker's test certificate asked for.

## How do you write a joinery line that can't be substituted?

Name five things:

1. The board, its standard and grade: "18 mm IS 303 BWP plywood carcass".
2. The thickness of each part, if carcass, shutters and back differ.
3. The finish inside and out: "1 mm laminate outside, 0.8 mm inside", or acrylic, veneer, PU.
4. The edge band: "2 mm PVC edge band".
5. The hardware make, or "[make] or equal" with the reference named.

How joinery is measured, net as fixed and by area with its thickness, is in [measurement rules](/boq/measurement-rules). The [checker](/boq/check) flags a joinery line missing any of these; the [item library](/boq/items) has a line to start from for each item.

## What does this guide not decide?

Which grade a job needs. Standards are cited by number and title from the BIS catalogue, not quoted; the standard governs. Which grade a job needs is a design decision this page does not make.

title: How interior work is measured for a BOQ (IS 1200)
answer: Floors, ceilings, paint and woodwork have an Indian Standard for measurement, IS 1200: measure net as fixed, deduct openings only above a set size, and price skirting by running length with its height stated. Modular kitchens and wardrobes have none, so a BOQ line must say its basis: the same wardrobe can be 60 sq ft or 8 running ft.

body:
## Which interior trades have a measurement standard?

IS 1200 is the Indian Standard method of measuring building work, in parts by trade. Four parts cover most of an interior job; modular furniture is not one of them.

| Work | Standard | Unit in the standard |
|---|---|---|
| False ceilings and wall linings | IS 1200 (Part 10) | square metres, measured flat |
| Floors, dado and skirting | IS 1200 (Part 11) | square metres; skirting in running metres |
| Paint on walls and ceilings | IS 1200 (Part 13) | square metres |
| Woodwork, panelling and joinery | IS 1200 (Part 21) | square metres for boarding, with its thickness |
| Modular kitchens, wardrobes, lofts | None | whatever the BOQ states |

Interior quotes in India are usually written in sq ft and running ft rather than the standard's metric units: 1 sq m is 10.764 sq ft, and 1 m is 3.281 ft. The rules below are the same in either unit.

## How are floors, dado and skirting measured?

Part 11 measures floor finishes and dado in square metres, and skirting in running metres with its height stated; mitres, stops and returned ends are part of the skirting item, not extra. Nothing is deducted for embedded items up to 0.1 m² each. A strip of finish 30 cm wide or less that doesn't match the general floor is measured by running length; wider than that, by area.

For a BOQ that means three lines, not one: the floor by area, the skirting by length with its height, and any border or threshold strip as its own line.

## How are false ceilings measured?

Part 10 measures ceilings flat, in square metres, net as fixed. An opening up to 0.4 m² (a light cut-out, a grille) is not deducted and not charged for; a bigger opening is deducted in full and the work of forming it is measured separately. Boarding on curved surfaces up to 15 cm wide is its own item.

Coves, drops and bands are not flat ceiling, which is why the [false ceiling items](/boq/items/false-ceiling) price them by running length: say their girth (height plus width) in the line.

## How is paint measured?

Part 13 measures walls, ceilings and sloping surfaces separately, and every item states the number of coats. Openings up to 0.5 m² each are not deducted, and their reveals are not added. A line reading "painting, 900 sq ft" leaves out both: which surfaces, and how many coats of what.

## How are woodwork and panelling measured?

Part 21 measures woodwork net as fixed: nothing is added for shape, joints or wastage. Boarding, which the standard says covers panelling, shelves and almirah linings, is measured in square metres with its finished thickness stated. Wastage belongs in the rate, not the quantity.

## How are modular kitchens, wardrobes and lofts measured?

No Indian Standard sets how modular units are measured, so the trade uses several bases, and two quotes on different bases can't be compared:

- **Kitchen cabinets**: usually by running length along the wall, base and wall units as separate lines, corners counted once. Say whether the plinth and back panels are included.
- **Wardrobes**: usually by front elevation, height × width. Say whether the loft, side panels and internal drawers are in it; lofts are often a separate line.
- **Tall units and accessories**: per unit, size stated.

The same wardrobe, 8 ft wide and 7 ft 6 in high, is 60 sq ft by elevation or 8 running ft along the wall. At ₹1,450 per sq ft it costs ₹87,000; quoted per running ft, the same price is ₹10,875 a foot. A BOQ that asks for "wardrobe, per sq ft" without saying which area gets prices that can't be put side by side.

Write the basis into every modular line, for example: "measured by front elevation area, excluding loft and drawers". The [BOQ checker](/boq/check) flags modular lines that don't, and its dimension box works out the quantity from `8' x 7'6"`.

## Which editions are these rules from?

Older public editions of IS 1200, so check the current one. The rules come from the public copies of IS 1200 Parts 10, 11, 13 and 21 linked below. They are older editions, and newer revisions may differ in detail; check the current edition in the BIS catalogue before relying on a figure in a contract. The modular bases are trade practice, not a standard. Each trade's items, with a line to start from, are in the [item library](/boq/items).

title: Variation orders in interior work, priced from the BOQ
answer: A variation order records a change after the BOQ is agreed: what was added, omitted or substituted, at what rate, and its effect on time and payment, signed before the work is done. CPWD's contract conditions price a changed item at its BOQ rate, a new item at a market rate claimed within 15 days, and extend time in proportion to the added cost.
description: How to record and price changes after an interior BOQ is agreed, using the CPWD contract's clause 12 as the model: rates, new items, time.

body:
## What is a variation order in interior work?

Once a client accepts a quotation built on a BOQ, every later change is a variation: an extra item, a line dropped, a material swapped, a quantity that grew on site. A [variation order](/systems/variation-order) writes that change down with its price and its effect on time before the work is done, so the final bill is the BOQ plus a short list of approved changes, not an argument.

In interior work most variations are substitutions (veneer instead of laminate, a different tile), additions (a loft nobody drew) and quantities that move once walls are measured.

## What can a private contract borrow from CPWD's clause 12?

A tested structure for pricing changes. Private interior contracts aren't bound by government rules, but the Central Public Works Department's General Conditions of Contract give a tested structure for changes. Clause 12 says, in short:

- **Changes are made in writing.** The engineer in charge may alter, omit, add or substitute work by a signed written instruction, and the changed work becomes part of the contract.
- **A changed item keeps its contract price.** Altered or substituted work is done on the same conditions, including price, as the main work, unless the rules below apply.
- **A new item gets a market rate, claimed quickly.** For an item not in the contract, the contractor claims a market rate within 15 days, backed by a rate analysis and invoices; the engineer decides the rate within 45 days.
- **Quantities far above the BOQ can be re-rated.** Where a contract item exceeds the limit set in the contract's schedule, the rate for the excess quantity can be revised the same way.
- **Time moves with cost.** The completion time is extended in proportion to the added cost against the original contract value, plus 25% of that extra time.

## What should a variation order record?

Seven things:

1. **Which line it changes**: the BOQ line number and its description, or "new item".
2. **What changes**: added, omitted, substituted or quantity revised, with the new description written as fully as a BOQ line (board and grade, thickness, finish, hardware, unit and measurement basis).
3. **The rate and where it comes from**: the BOQ rate if the item is already in the BOQ; a new rate with its rate analysis if it isn't.
4. **The amount, plus or minus**, and GST on it.
5. **Effect on time**: the extra days, worked out the same way as clause 12 or as agreed.
6. **Effect on payment**: which payment stage it is billed with.
7. **Signatures and date**, before the work starts.

## How is a change priced from the BOQ?

Most of the price is already in the BOQ. A wardrobe that grows from 60 to 72 sq ft by front elevation is 12 more sq ft at the agreed rate. A swap from laminate to veneer shutters is the difference between two rates, each built from material, labour and wastage. An omission is a credit at the BOQ rate.

This only works if the BOQ line said what was priced. "Wardrobe, per sq ft" gives nothing to price a change against; a line that names the board, thickness, finish, hardware and [measurement basis](/systems/measurement-basis) does. The [measurement rules](/boq/measurement-rules) and [material specifications](/boq/material-specifications) are where those lines are settled.

## When should variation rules be agreed?

Before the first change. Put the variation rules in the quotation's terms: changes only in writing, the BOQ rate for listed items, how a new item is priced, and how much quantity can grow before its rate is reopened. Ahrom Labs' own default terms for a design studio's quotations include "work not listed here, or changed after acceptance, is quoted separately as a variation".

## Does CPWD's clause 12 bind a private interior job?

No. The clause 12 summary is from the CPWD General Conditions of Contract for construction works, April 2026 edition; it binds government works under that contract, not a private interior job. Use it as a model and put your own rules in your contract. The schedule limits it refers to vary by contract and are not given here.

title: What is a BOQ? BOQ vs estimate, quotation and BOM

Contractors fill in the rates, so three quotes can be compared line by line. An estimate is the expected cost, a quotation is a priced offer, and a BOM lists the parts of one product.

body:
## What is a BOQ?

A [BOQ](/systems/bill-of-quantities) is the list of work, not the price of it ([what one looks like in Excel](/boq/template)). Each line names one item (a wardrobe, a ceiling, a wiring point), says what it is made of, gives the unit it is measured in and the quantity measured from the drawings. The rate and amount columns stay empty until someone prices them.

Its job is to make prices comparable. When three contractors price the same lines, the quotes differ only in rates, and a cheap quote can't hide a thinner board or a missing loft.

## BOQ vs BOM, estimate and quotation: what is the difference?

| Document | Who makes it | What it holds | Binding? |
|---|---|---|---|
| BOQ | Designer or quantity surveyor | Items, descriptions, units, quantities | No; it is the basis for prices |
| Estimate | Designer or owner | The BOQ with expected rates: what the job should cost | No; internal |
| Quotation | Contractor or the design-build studio | Rates, amounts, taxes, terms, validity | Yes, once accepted |
| BOM | Manufacturer or workshop | Every part and material to make one product | No; it drives buying and cutting |

The BOM and the BOQ meet in a workshop. The client's BOQ has one line for a wardrobe priced by area; the workshop's BOM for that wardrobe lists the sheets of plywood, the laminate, the edge band and each hinge.

## What are a rate analysis and a schedule of rates?

A rate analysis breaks one item's rate into material, labour, wastage, overheads and profit. It is how a contractor arrives at the rate in a BOQ line, and how a designer checks one that looks too low.

A schedule of rates is a published list of item rates. For central government works, the Central Public Works Department publishes the Delhi Schedule of Rates (DSR). It is a reference for how items are described and priced in government work, not a price list for private interiors in another city.

## What are lump sums, provisional sums and PC sums?

Three ways to price work that isn't measured line by line:

- **Lump sum**: one price for a defined scope ("bathroom CP fittings, LS"). Quick to write, but it hides what's inside; split it into named items wherever you can. CPWD's contract conditions do the same in clause 27: where an estimate includes a lump sum for part of the work, the contractor is paid for the items involved at the contract's own rates.
- **Provisional sum**: an allowance for work not yet defined, adjusted when it is.
- **Prime cost (PC) sum**: an allowance for something the client will choose later, such as tiles at a stated rate per sq ft, adjusted to the actual price.

When a provisional or PC sum is settled, or anything else changes after the BOQ is agreed, it is recorded as a [variation order](/boq/variation-orders).

## Does this page give rates?

No. This page explains the documents; it does not give rates. How each interior item is measured and specified is in the [item library](/boq/items), and the [checker](/boq/check) reads a BOQ from Excel and shows what each line leaves open.

body:
## Which compliance rules apply to my business?

Most rules turn on two facts: whether the business is a company, and its turnover. The [requirements builder](/erp/check) applies these for you.

| Rule | Applies when | What the ERP must do |
|---|---|---|
| Audit trail | A company keeps its books in software | Log every change with its date; can't be switched off |
| E-invoice (IRN) | Aggregate turnover above ₹5 crore in any year since 2017-18 | Get an IRN for each B2B invoice, credit and debit note |
| 30-day IRP limit | Annual aggregate turnover ₹10 crore and above | Report each e-invoice within 30 days of its date |
| E-way bill | Goods move with a consignment value above ₹50,000 | Produce the e-way bill from the dispatch |
| MSME payment limit | Buying from a micro or small enterprise | Track each bill's due date, at most 45 days from acceptance |
| TDS on purchase of goods | A buyer with turnover above ₹10 crore in the previous year | Track each seller's yearly total; deduct beyond ₹50 lakh |
| Personal data | Holding digital personal data of staff, customers or contacts | Reasonable security safeguards; breaches can be traced (rules on how: from May 2027) |

## Does my ERP need an audit trail?

Yes, if your business is a company: since 1 April 2023, a company that keeps its books in accounting software must use software that records an [audit trail](/systems/audit-trail) of every transaction: an edit log of each change, with its date, that cannot be disabled. The rule is a proviso to rule 3(1) of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014, inserted in March 2021 and deferred twice to 1 April 2023. The company's auditor reports on it.

For an ERP that keeps the books, this means the old value, the new value, who changed it and when, for every entry, with no setting anywhere that turns it off. It also means no gap at cutover: the trail has to run through the move from the old system to the new one. See the [audit-trail requirement](/erp/requirements#accounts-audit-trail).

## When must an ERP generate e-invoices, and what is the 30-day limit?

From 1 August 2023, registered persons whose aggregate turnover exceeded ₹5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18 must [e-invoice](/systems/e-invoice): each B2B invoice, credit note and debit note is registered on the invoice registration portal (IRP), which returns an IRN and a signed QR code. Notification 10/2023–Central Tax lowered the threshold from ₹10 crore.

From 1 April 2025, taxpayers with annual aggregate turnover of ₹10 crore and above cannot report a document to the IRP more than 30 days after its date; the portal refuses it. An ERP for such a business should show which invoices are still unreported and how many days each has left. See the [e-invoice requirements](/erp/requirements#accounts-e-invoice).

## When is an e-way bill needed?

Under rule 138 of the CGST Rules, an [e-way bill](/systems/e-way-bill) is needed before goods move with a consignment value exceeding ₹50,000. The ERP should produce it from the invoice and the dispatch, not have someone retype the consignment into the portal at the gate. See the [e-way bill requirement](/erp/requirements#dispatch-eway-bill).

## How long can I take to pay an MSME supplier?

At most 45 days from acceptance. Section 15 of the MSMED Act, 2006 (the [MSME payment rule](/systems/msme-payment-rule)) requires a buyer to pay a micro or small enterprise supplier by the agreed date, and the agreed period can never exceed 45 days from acceptance; with no written agreement, the Act's appointed day applies. Section 16 adds compound interest on late payment.

The Income-tax Act, 2025, in section 37(2)(g), allows the deduction for an amount owed to such a supplier only when it is actually paid, if it is paid beyond that limit, and the usual grace until the return due date doesn't apply to it. So the ERP needs to know which suppliers are micro or small enterprises, and show each of their bills with its due date. How the rule applies to a particular business, a trader for example, is a question for your CA. See the [MSME requirements](/erp/requirements#purchase-msme-due-dates).

## When must a buyer deduct TDS on purchase of goods?

Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, a buyer whose turnover exceeded ₹10 crore in the preceding tax year deducts tax on payments to a seller for goods beyond ₹50 lakh in the year ([TDS on purchases](/systems/tds-on-purchases)) (section 393(1), table row 8(ii), formerly section 194Q). The provision is a table, so it is cited here rather than quoted: read row 8(ii) and its note in the Act. The ERP has to keep each seller's running total for the year and start deducting on the bill that crosses it. See the [TDS requirement](/erp/requirements#accounts-tds-purchases).

## What does the DPDP Act require of an ERP?

Reasonable security safeguards and a way to report a breach. A business holding digital personal data, of employees, customers or contacts, is a data fiduciary under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. Section 8 requires reasonable security safeguards to prevent a personal data breach and intimation of a breach in the prescribed way. For an ERP, that means access to personal details limited by role and logged, and a way to see who saw what. The Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (13 November 2025) set out how: the safeguards (rule 6) and breach intimation, including a detailed report to the Board within 72 hours (rule 7), come into force eighteen months after publication, in May 2027 (rule 1(4)). The Act's own sections are brought into force by separate notification, so check which are in force when you buy. If the system comes with an AI assistant, see [what it sends out](/ai-assistant/data-safety). See the [personal-data requirement](/erp/requirements#nonfunctional-personal-data).

## When did each rule start?

Between 2018 and 2026:

| Date | Change |
|---|---|
| 7 Mar 2018 | Rule 138 substituted: e-way bill above ₹50,000 |
| 24 Mar 2021 | Audit-trail proviso added to the Companies (Accounts) Rules |
| 31 Mar 2022 | Audit trail deferred to financial years from 1 April 2023 |
| 1 Aug 2023 | E-invoice threshold lowered to ₹5 crore |
| 11 Aug 2023 | Digital Personal Data Protection Act published |
| 1 Apr 2025 | 30-day IRP reporting limit extended to ₹10 crore and above |
| 1 Apr 2026 | Income-tax Act, 2025 in force: MSME rule in section 37(2)(g), TDS on goods in section 393 |

## How do I check that a vendor meets these rules?

Ask the vendor to do each test on the checklist, in front of you: change an entry and show the audit trail; generate an IRN for a test invoice; list the invoices that are near the 30-day limit; produce an e-way bill from a dispatch; show an MSME supplier's bills with due dates. A vendor who can't show it doesn't have it yet. Ahrom Labs states its own gaps the same way: it has not yet built an IRP connection, and its e-way bill client is built but not yet live.

body:
## Who owns the code of a custom ERP?

Either you or the vendor, and the contract should say which. Custom software in India is sold in one of two ways, and buyers often don't find out which until they try to leave.

| | You own the code | The vendor licenses it |
|---|---|---|
| What you pay for | The build, and the code is handed over | A working system and a licence to use it |
| After the build | You can take it to any developer | The licence runs with the maintenance contract |
| Usually costs | More up front, plus whoever maintains it | Less up front, plus the annual contract |
| Risk to watch | Code nobody else can maintain without documentation | Losing the licence if the contract ends |

Neither is wrong. What is wrong is not knowing which one you signed.

## Which clauses should an ERP contract settle before the build?

Eight, from code ownership to personal data:

1. **Ownership.** Who owns the source code and the software. If it's licensed, what the licence covers and for how long. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#contract-ownership))
2. **Your data.** That you can export all your business data, in standard formats, at any time, including at the end. Data you can't take out ties you tighter than any clause. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#nonfunctional-data-export))
3. **Pricing.** Fixed price per phase, quoted before each phase starts, or time and materials, with a cap. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#contract-fixed-phases))
4. **Changes.** How a change is written down, priced and agreed before it is built. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#contract-changes))
5. **The maintenance contract.** What it covers (licence, hosting, fixes, small changes), what it costs per year, and what is quoted separately. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#contract-amc-scope))
6. **Support.** Response time in writing, and documentation that lets another developer take the system over. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#nonfunctional-support))
7. **Hosting and storage.** Who pays for the server and the storage, and whether storage costs are passed on at the provider's price.
8. **Personal data.** If the vendor processes personal data on your behalf (staff, customers, contacts), the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 requires a valid contract for that: section 8(2). Name the vendor's duties for safeguards and breach intimation in it.

## How does Ahrom Labs handle code, maintenance and data?

Ahrom Labs owns the code and licenses it to you while the maintenance contract runs, and your data is yours. Stated plainly, as on the [engagement page](/engagement):

- **Ahrom Labs owns the code.** You get a working system and a licence to use it for as long as the annual maintenance contract runs; the source code stays with Ahrom Labs. If the contract stops, the licence ends with it.
- **Your data is yours** and can be exported at any time.
- **Fixed price per phase**, after a short fixed-fee modeling phase; a change is priced and agreed before it is built.
- **The AMC is 15–21% of the project value per year**, covering the licence, the server, fixes and small changes; a new module is its own phase.
- **Support** requests are answered within 48 hours at most, and every system ships with a system document any developer or agent can pick it up from.

If you need to own the code outright, say so before the build; it changes the price and the hand-over, and it is better settled first than discovered later.

title: ERP implementation plan: phases from mapping the business to go-live
metaTitle: ERP implementation plan: phases from mapping to go-live
answer: A custom ERP goes live in phases, each in use before the next starts: a short modeling phase that maps the business and ends with a dated, fixed-price plan; then the records that must be right; then the daily work of each department; then reports and AI. Data migration is its own scoped piece of work, and the requirements' tests are the acceptance tests for each phase.
description: ERP implementation plan for Indian manufacturers and traders: phases from modeling to go-live, migration, acceptance tests, timeline and cost.

image.alt: A path of five stepping stones leading to a flag.

body:
## Why run an ERP project in phases?

So that each phase is in use before the next one starts, which catches a wrong assumption early. ERP projects in Indian SMEs usually fail the same way: people go back to Excel and WhatsApp because the system doesn't match how the business runs, and the old data turns out messier than anyone planned for. Phases that each go live and get used before the next one starts catch both early. You never pay for months of work you can't see, and a wrong assumption costs a phase, not the project.

## What are the phases of an ERP implementation?

Modeling first, then the records that must be right, then everything else, each going live before the next:

| Phase | What it delivers | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| 0. Modeling | A map of the business (entities, workflows, approvals, rules) and a dated plan with a fixed price per phase | The owner agrees the map and the plan |
| 1. Records that must be right | Masters, stock, opening balances, the ledger or the Tally link; migration of what's needed | Counts and balances tie to the old system |
| 2. Daily work, department by department | Sales, purchase, stores, production, dispatch, accounts, as the plan orders them | Each department works in the system, not beside it |
| 3. Portals | Customer and supplier access | Customers and suppliers use their links |
| 4. Reports and AI | Dashboards from the same records; assistants and document reading with human review | Figures trace to records; AI answers match the reports |

The order inside phase 2 comes from the map: whatever the business can least afford to get wrong goes first.

## How should data migration be handled?

As its own piece of work: migration is scoped and quoted separately, before it starts, rather than discovered halfway. Every import is checked against its source, doubtful rows are held for a person, and each import is tagged so it can be removed as one batch. See [moving from Tally](/erp/tally-migration).

## How do I test each phase before signing it off?

With the requirements themselves: every line on the [requirements checklist](/erp/requirements) has a test. Before a phase is signed off, run the tests for the lines it covers, on your own data. The same tests made the [vendor demo script](/erp/vendor-demo-script); using them again at go-live is how you find out whether what was shown is what was built.

## How long does an ERP implementation take?

It depends on how new the problem is. Something already built for another business can ship in days or weeks; genuinely new ground takes a couple of months, delivered in phases so part of it is in use early. The modeling phase ends with a date for each phase, so you know the timeline before you commit to the build.

## What does a custom ERP cost in India?

Published 2026 guides from other firms put a custom ERP for a small Indian manufacturer at roughly ₹3–15 lakh, and a fuller build for a mid-sized manufacturer at ₹15–40 lakh. Those are market figures, not a price list: two businesses that both want "an ERP" can need very different systems, which is why the price is fixed per phase only after the modeling phase. Maintenance after go-live usually runs as an annual contract. Ahrom Labs' terms, and the sources for those ranges, are on the [engagement page](/engagement); what to settle in the contract is in the [contract checklist](/erp/contract-checklist).

## What should the written plan look like?

One line per phase. Write the plan as a table: phase, what it delivers, the requirement lines it covers, the acceptance tests, the date, the price. If a vendor can't fill that table before the build, the plan isn't ready.

## What should an interior design firm require first?

BOQ quotations, project blockers, vendor rate checks, payroll and two companies' books:

1. **Quotations from a BOQ**, with revisions kept and the accepted one turned into the order without retyping. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#sales-quotation-format)) How to write the BOQ itself is in the [interior BOQ guide](/boq).
2. **What each project is waiting on**: material, drawing, approval or payment, worked out fresh each time. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#production-blockers))
3. **Vendor and freight charges checked** against agreed rates, with overcharges flagged. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#purchase-rate-check))
4. **Labour logged against each job**, so job costs include it. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#payroll-work-logs))
5. **Payroll computed** from attendance, rates and advances, never typed. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#payroll-computed))
6. **Two companies, one system**: each invoice under its own company's letterhead and GSTIN, from one client list. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#sales-multi-company))
7. **Staff see only their own cash entries**, and bank data is refused to them by the system. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#nonfunctional-role-access))

## Which rules usually apply?

The audit trail if you are a company, e-invoicing by turnover, and the MSME payment limit:

- **Being a company:** the books need an [audit trail](/systems/audit-trail). ([audit trail](/erp/requirements#accounts-audit-trail))
- **Above ₹5 crore:** e-invoices for B2B work. ([e-invoice](/erp/requirements#accounts-e-invoice))
- **Paying micro and small vendors:** due dates at most 45 days from acceptance. ([MSME](/erp/requirements#purchase-msme-due-dates))

All of them, quoted from the official text: [compliance requirements](/erp/compliance).

## What does this look like in a running system?

Savistar, an interior design studio, and Saag, its sister furniture workshop, run one system: projects and site visits for Savistar, workshop orders for Saag, and one combined finance ledger. Each invoice picks its own company's letterhead, logo and GSTIN; vendor and freight charges are checked against reference rates; payroll is days × rate − advances, never typed; and an AI assistant answers from their own records in English or Hinglish. Quotations are built from a BOQ library, with payment stages that become invoices. See [software for interior design firms](/industries/interior-design-and-furniture), or try the [interiors demo](https://interiors-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo), where one freight trip is overcharged on purpose.

## How do I build my own requirements list?

If the system will have an AI assistant, [what it should answer for this kind of business](/ai-assistant/interior-design-firms) lists the questions, with what Atelier AI answers today.

title: Is your business ready for an ERP? A 10-question self-check
answer: A business is ready for an ERP when someone owns each process, the masters are clean enough to load, the owner will decide disputes between departments, and people will record work where it happens. Ten questions, each with what to fix first if the answer is no.
description: ERP readiness checklist for Indian manufacturers and traders: ten questions on processes, masters, owners and data, and what to fix first.

image.alt: A hand placing the top block on a small pyramid of building blocks.

body:
## What are the ten readiness questions?

Ten yes-or-no questions on processes, owners, masters, stock, compliance and Tally; each no is something to fix before, or as the first phase of, any system.

1. **Can you draw how an order moves**, from enquiry to payment, with who does what at each step? If not, that map is the first piece of work; a system built on the wrong picture makes the workarounds faster.
2. **Does each process have one owner** who can say how it should work? Without one, the system inherits every disagreement.
3. **Are your masters clean?** One record per customer, supplier and item, with GSTINs and HSN codes that are right. Duplicates in Tally become duplicates in the ERP.
4. **Do you know your stock** to the level you pick and ship (a reel, a box, a plate), or only as totals? If only totals, plan a stock count before go-live.
5. **Is there one place for each number?** If the same figure lives in Tally, a spreadsheet and someone's notebook, decide now which one is the truth.
6. **Will people record work where it happens**, on a phone on the floor or at site, rather than at a desk at day end?
7. **Will the owner decide** when sales and production disagree about how something should work? Systems fail more often from undecided questions than from code.
8. **Do you know which compliance rules apply?** Turnover decides [e-invoicing](/systems/e-invoice) and its 30-day limit; being a company decides the [audit trail](/systems/audit-trail). See [compliance requirements](/erp/compliance).
9. **Have you decided about Tally?** Keep it as the books, or move the books into the new system. See [moving from Tally](/erp/tally-migration).
10. **Can you name the first thing the system must get right?** The records that must be right come first; everything else is a later phase.

## How do I score the answers?

Count the yes answers:

- **8 to 10 yes:** ready. Write your requirements with the [builder](/erp/check) and start talking to vendors.
- **5 to 7:** ready if the first phase is mapping the business and cleaning masters, not building screens.
- **Under 5:** start with the map. Buying a system before the processes are decided is how ERP projects stall.

## Why fix these before buying software?

Because systems fail more often from undecided questions than from code. Ahrom Labs starts every engagement with a short modeling phase that answers most of these questions: what exists, who owns it, which records must be right, and what each phase delivers. You keep the model and the plan whether or not you continue. See [how an engagement runs](/engagement) and the [requirements checklist](/erp/requirements).

body:
## How should I use an ERP selection matrix?

For the first cut only: which options to invite at all. Don't pick a system from a feature table, this one included. Every option below can be made to look good in a demo. Pick from your own requirements:

1. Build your list with the [requirements builder](/erp/check) and set a priority on each line.
2. Send the same [Excel template](/erp/template) to each option, one copy per vendor. It scores Yes, Partly and No against your priorities.
3. Make each vendor do the [demo tests](/erp/vendor-demo-script) for your Must lines. A yes you didn't see counts as partly.

The table below is for the first cut: which options to invite at all. Each fact is from the product's own documentation, linked under sources.

## How do Tally, ERPNext, Odoo, SAP Business One and custom compare?

On licence, hosting, Indian compliance and fit, from each product's own documentation:

| | TallyPrime | ERPNext | Odoo | SAP Business One | Custom-built |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| What it is | Accounting and inventory software from Tally Solutions | Open-source ERP from Frappe | ERP suite of apps, Community and Enterprise editions | SAP's ERP for small businesses | A system built around your process |
| Licence | Proprietary licence | GPL-3.0 (open source) | Community: LGPLv3; Enterprise: Odoo's own licence | Proprietary licence | As your contract says: you own the code, or a licence runs with maintenance |
| Where it runs | Your PC or server; TallyPrime's integration gateway listens only on that machine | Self-hosted or Frappe Cloud | Odoo Online, Odoo.sh or on-premise | Cloud or on-premise | Wherever it's built for |
| E-invoice and e-way bill | Built in: IRN, QR code and e-way bill from the sales voucher | Through the India Compliance app (GST, e-invoice, e-way bill, TDS) | India localization modules for e-invoicing (from 15.0) and e-way bill | Through India localization and partner add-ons; check with your partner | Built to the NIC specs, or not at all; ask |
| Audit trail (edit log) | Edit log; a separate release keeps it always on | Check it meets the rule | Check it meets the rule | Check it meets the rule | Must be built in and can't be switched off |
| Fit to your process | You adapt to it | Configurable; customised by developers | Configurable; customised by developers or partners | Configured by partners | The process is modeled first, then built |
| Works alongside Tally | Is Tally | Replaces it, or runs beside it with an integration | Replaces it, or runs beside it with an integration | Replaces it, or runs beside it with an integration | Either: posts into Tally, or keeps the books itself |

"Check it meets the rule" means the product's documentation we read doesn't say, in plain terms, that the edit log meets the [audit-trail rule](/erp/compliance): a log of every change with its date that can't be disabled. Ask the vendor to show it.

## When does each option tend to fit?

By where the business's work happens:

- **TallyPrime alone**: accounting-led businesses whose operations fit in its inventory, and who mainly need GST done right. When it stops being enough is in [seven signs you've outgrown Tally](/notes/outgrown-tally-signs).
- **ERPNext or Odoo**: businesses whose processes are close to the standard modules, with a partner or in-house developer to configure and maintain them.
- **SAP Business One**: small businesses that want an established vendor and a partner-led implementation.
- **Custom**: when the process is the business's edge, the standard modules force workarounds, or the system has to do something no package does (an IBR statutory folder from certificates, reel-level reservations, two companies on one ledger).

The longer comparison for manufacturers is [Tally, ERPNext, Odoo or a custom ERP](/notes/tally-vs-erpnext-vs-custom-erp).

## What does the matrix leave out?

Price, deliberately: licence, implementation and maintenance costs change by edition, users and partner, and a number here would be wrong for most readers. Get quotes against the same requirements list, and settle ownership and data export before signing: see the [contract checklist](/erp/contract-checklist). Ahrom Labs builds custom systems, so read this page as a builder's view; the facts about each product are from its own documentation.

body:
## What should a small manufacturer require first?

The lines a small manufacturer can least afford to get wrong, in the order they usually go live. Each links to its test.

1. **Your BOMs, from Excel.** Import the sheets you already keep, matched to the item master; a likely typo suggested, never silently corrected. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#production-bom-import))
2. **A released BOM is frozen.** Purchase and stores work from a version, not a moving sheet. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#production-bom-release))
3. **Shortfalls become purchase requests**, after stock and usable remnants are counted. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#purchase-need-to-request))
4. **Remnants go back into stock**, with weights from dimensions, offered to waiting BOM lines before anything is bought. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#production-cutting-remnants))
5. **Jobs costed from actual use**, material and labour. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#production-costing-from-use))
6. **What each job is waiting on**, worked out fresh, not typed. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#production-blockers))
7. **Certificates kept once and linked to what they cover**, with any link that ends in statutory paperwork confirmed by a person. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#quality-confirmed-links))

## Which rules does turnover bring in?

It depends on turnover and on being a company:

- **Being a company:** the books need an [audit trail](/systems/audit-trail) that can't be switched off. ([audit trail](/erp/requirements#accounts-audit-trail))
- **Above ₹5 crore:** e-invoices for B2B sales; **at ₹10 crore and above:** reported within 30 days. ([e-invoice](/erp/requirements#accounts-e-invoice))
- **Buying from micro and small enterprises:** due dates at most 45 days from acceptance. ([MSME](/erp/requirements#purchase-msme-due-dates))

All of them, quoted from the official text, are in [compliance requirements](/erp/compliance).

## What does this look like in a running system?

At a boiler and pressure-vessel manufacturer, Ahrom Labs' system imported six of the client's real BOM files through the interface, traces each plate and section through cutting, and assembled each boiler's [IBR statutory folder](/systems/ibr-statutory-folder) from a bank of [material test certificates](/systems/material-test-certificate). In a live cut test, a 157.00 kg plate became 127.17 kg used, 15.70 kg remnant and 14.13 kg scrap, conserved exactly. The same system keeps the books: GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, TDS and 23 reports, with Tally optional. See [ERP for boiler and pressure-vessel manufacturers](/industries/boiler-pressure-vessel-manufacturing), or try it with twelve sample logins, one per department, at the [manufacturing demo](https://boiler-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo).

## How do I build my own requirements list?

The [requirements builder](/erp/check) with "Manufacturing" selected gives the full list for your turnover and whether Tally stays, ready to send to vendors.

If the system will have an AI assistant, [what it should answer for this kind of business](/ai-assistant/manufacturers) lists the questions, with what Ember AI answers today.

title: Moving from Tally to an ERP: what to migrate and how to check it
metaTitle: Moving from Tally to an ERP: what to migrate and check
answer: Decide first whether Tally stays as the books or goes. Then move masters, opening balances, outstanding bills, stock with its batches, and the history people actually look up, each checked against its source: count the rows, hold anything that matches two records for a person, and tag every import so it can be removed as a batch. Keep the audit trail unbroken through the switch.
description: How to move from Tally to an ERP in India: keep Tally or replace it, what to migrate, how to check each import, and the audit-trail rule at cutover.

body:
## Should Tally stay or go when you move to an ERP?

Either works, and the choice decides what you migrate: if Tally stays as the books, only masters and open items move; if the ERP takes the books, ledgers and returns move too.

- **Tally stays as the books.** The ERP runs sales, stock and operations, and posts approved invoices into TallyPrime as vouchers. Your accountant keeps working in Tally. Very little accounting history moves; what moves is masters and open items. LS Technologies runs this way: approved invoices reach TallyPrime within 30 seconds, and every posted voucher is checked against Tally's own data.
- **The ERP keeps the books.** Ledgers, GST returns and TDS move into the ERP, and Tally becomes optional or goes. More moves, and the [audit trail](/systems/audit-trail) has to carry across. A boiler manufacturer Ahrom Labs built for runs this way, with GSTR-1, GSTR-3B and TDS from the operations system.

How each connection to Tally works, and why TallyPrime needs an agent on its own PC, is in [four ways to connect a business system to TallyPrime](/notes/connecting-tallyprime-four-ways).

## What data should move from Tally to the ERP?

Masters, opening balances, outstanding bills, stock and the history people look up, each checked against Tally:

| What | Why it matters | How to check it |
|---|---|---|
| Ledger and party masters | Every transaction hangs off them | Count before and after; no duplicates by GSTIN |
| Item masters, with units and HSN | Stock and tax depend on them | Count; every HSN valid; units consistent |
| Opening balances | The books must agree on day one | Trial balance in the ERP equals Tally's on the cutover date |
| Outstanding bills (receivable and payable) | Collections and payments continue | Each party's total matches Tally's outstanding |
| Stock, with batches or units | Reservations and costing need it | Quantity and value per item match; batches or units as labelled |
| GST history you look up | Returns and notices refer back | The periods you need, read-only, with their filing status |
| Sales history (enquiries, quotations, orders) | Sales can't work without it | Row counts; doubtful rows held, not guessed |

## How do you check each import?

With three rules, from moving five years of a manufacturer's sales history (see [the note](/notes/sales-history-moved-without-guessing)):

1. **Check the file against itself first.** A broken export had shifted 154 of 20,167 diary rows by a column or two; read naively, they would have lost their status. All 20,167 were recovered by checking each row's known last columns.
2. **Hold, don't guess.** A quotation that matched no customer, or more than one, went to a review list: 2,221 matched exactly one customer and came in; 303 waited for a person.
3. **Tag every import.** Each row carries the import it came from, so a batch found wrong later can be removed as one.

## How do you keep the audit trail unbroken at cutover?

Close a period in Tally and start the ERP's trail from the first entry after it. A company keeping its books in software must have an audit trail for every financial year from 1 April 2023 (the date was substituted by the Companies (Accounts) Second Amendment Rules, 2022). Plan the cutover so the trail doesn't break: close a period in Tally, move balances as at that date, and start the ERP's trail from the first entry after. Keep Tally's data for the years before, read-only, for the auditor. See the [audit-trail requirement](/erp/requirements#accounts-audit-trail-date).

## In what order should a Tally migration run?

Masters first, history last:

1. Freeze masters for a week; clean duplicates in Tally first.
2. Move masters, then check counts.
3. Pick a cutover date at a period end.
4. Move opening balances and outstanding bills as at that date; tie the trial balance.
5. Move stock and check quantity and value per item.
6. Run both systems for one cycle if Tally stays as the books; compare.
7. Move history last, read-only, and hold doubtful rows for a person.

See also the [migration requirement](/erp/requirements#sales-history-migration) and the [Tally integration requirements](/erp/requirements#integrations-tally).

body:
## What does Tally do well?

TallyPrime is accounting software first: ledgers and vouchers, GST with e-invoicing and e-way bills, TDS, and
stock. Most Indian accountants know it, your CA can read it, and it runs on one PC
(Silver) or many (Gold). For a business whose work is buying, selling and keeping books, it is hard to beat on cost
and familiarity.

## Where does Tally stop being enough?

The trouble starts when the work around the books lives elsewhere: enquiries in WhatsApp, quotations in Word,
production in Excel, site measurements on paper, stock reserved for orders in someone's head. Then the same
invoice is typed twice, the numbers in Tally arrive days after the work, and nobody outside accounts can see an
order's status. The note [seven signs a business has outgrown Tally](/notes/outgrown-tally-signs) lists them with
what fixed each.

## What are the options besides replacing Tally?

Three: customise Tally with TDL, build an operations system beside it that posts vouchers into it, or replace it.

| | Keep Tally, customise it | Build beside Tally | Replace Tally |
|---|---|---|---|
| What changes | TDL add-ons inside Tally: fields, reports, checks | An operations system for sales, stores, production or projects; vouchers posted into Tally | One system holds operations and the books |
| Tally stays the books | Yes | Yes | No |
| Accountants' habits | Unchanged | Unchanged | Retrained |
| Fits | Small extra fields, reports, validations | Work that happens outside accounts, by people who don't use Tally | Groups that need one ledger with operations, or whose books depend on operational detail |
| Risk | Low; limited by what Tally's screens can hold | Medium; the link to Tally has to be reliable | Highest; a full migration and cutover |

Tally supports both of the first two: TDL, its own language, extends Tally from inside, and Tally documents
integration with outside systems over its interfaces. How the voucher link is built, and how failures are caught,
is in [connecting to TallyPrime four ways](/notes/connecting-tallyprime-four-ways) and
[posting vouchers into Tally](/notes/tally-voucher-posting).

## How do I decide between them?

By where your work is recorded today:

1. List where each step of your work is recorded today, from enquiry to payment.
2. If almost everything is already in Tally, customise it.
3. If most steps happen outside Tally, by people who aren't accountants, build beside it and keep Tally.
4. Replace Tally only if you need what it can't hold in the books themselves, and plan the move with
   [moving from Tally to an ERP](/erp/tally-migration).

Whichever you pick, test it with the [vendor demo script](/erp/vendor-demo-script) on your own transactions, and
score the options with the [selection matrix](/erp/selection-matrix).

## Does the audit-trail rule apply to Tally and to a custom ERP?

Yes, to both. For a company, the Companies (Accounts) Rules require accounting software that records an audit trail of every
transaction, with an edit log, and that the audit trail can't be disabled. Check that your Tally setup meets it,
and a custom system that holds books, or posts entries that become books, must meet it too. See
[ERP compliance in India](/erp/compliance).

## What does each option cost?

Tally's prices are on its site and change with each plan; a system beside it is a project. For how we scope one
and what you own, see [how an engagement works](/engagement). The cost that's easy to miss is the one you
already pay: the hours spent typing the same data twice.

body:
## What should a trading business require first?

Stock by the unit you ship, reservations, scanning, AI-read documents and Tally posting:

1. **Stock by the unit you ship**: a reel, a box, a carton, each with its own label, not only a total. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#stores-unit-level))
2. **Reserved against each order line**, so a reserved unit can't go to another customer without a manager's override. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#stores-reservations))
3. **Moved by scanning**, in, out and between stores, including a partner's. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#stores-scan-moves))
4. **Staff entries approved** before they change stock. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#stores-approval))
5. **Purchase documents read by AI and checked by a person**: invoices, freight bills, bills of entry, bank statements. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#reporting-extraction-review))
6. **Every supplier bill matched** to its order and what was received. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#purchase-three-way-match))
7. **Invoices into Tally automatically**, each checked against Tally's own data, if Tally stays as the books. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#accounts-tally-posting))
8. **Customers follow their own orders** on a portal that never shows stock or other customers. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#portals-no-stock-exposure))

## Which rules does turnover bring in?

E-invoicing, the 30-day IRP limit and TDS on goods, by turnover:

- **Above ₹5 crore:** e-invoices; **at ₹10 crore and above:** reported within 30 days. ([e-invoice](/erp/requirements#accounts-e-invoice))
- **As a buyer with turnover above ₹10 crore:** [TDS on purchases](/systems/tds-on-purchases) from a seller beyond ₹50 lakh in the year. ([TDS on purchases](/erp/requirements#accounts-tds-purchases))
- **Goods moving above ₹50,000:** [e-way bills](/systems/e-way-bill). ([e-way bill](/erp/requirements#dispatch-eway-bill))

All of them, quoted from the official text: [compliance requirements](/erp/compliance).

## What does this look like in a running system?

At LS Technologies, an electronics-component importer and trader, each reel carries its own QR label; 5,256 live reels moved to a two-store model with none lost. Reels are reserved per customer PO line, oldest first. Five document types, bills of entry included, are read by AI at 88–95% zero-correction, each approved by a person, and approved invoices post into TallyPrime as vouchers within 30 seconds. See [software for electronics-component traders](/industries/electronics-component-trading), or scan reels yourself in the [trading demo](https://electronics-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo).

## How do I build my own requirements list?

The [requirements builder](/erp/check) with "Trading and distribution" selected gives the full list for your turnover and whether Tally stays.

If the system will have an AI assistant, [what it should answer for this kind of business](/ai-assistant/trading-distribution) lists the questions, with what Ohm AI answers today.

title: ERP vendor demo script: what to make every vendor show you
answer: Don't let an ERP vendor run their own demo. Bring your own data, give them a list of tests, and watch them do each one: change an entry and show the audit trail, reserve stock and try to ship it elsewhere, post an invoice to Tally and delete it there. A yes you didn't see demonstrated is a partly.
description: ERP vendor demo script for Indian manufacturers and traders: the tests to make every vendor do in front of you, by department, and red flags.

image.alt: A laptop on a stand showing a dashboard, with a stopwatch beside it.

body:
## How should I run an ERP vendor demo?

On your own tests and data, sent ahead, not on the vendor's script. A vendor's own demo shows what their product does well, on data made to look good. Yours should show whether it does what your business needs, on data that looks like yours.

1. **Send the tests a week ahead.** The vendor should know what they'll be asked; a vendor who can't prepare for a known test won't handle an unknown one.
2. **Bring your own data.** A real BOM, a real supplier bill, ten real stock items. Sample data hides the edge cases you live with.
3. **You drive, or you call every click.** Watching a smooth run-through tells you little; asking "now change that" tells you a lot.
4. **Score as you go.** Yes only for what you saw done. Use the [Excel template](/erp/template): it has a column for each answer and scores vendors for you.
5. **Keep the script.** The same tests are your acceptance tests before go-live.

## Which tests should every vendor do in front of me?

The ones most often promised and least often shown, by department. Pick the ones that apply from the [requirements builder](/erp/check). These are the ones most often promised and least often shown.

**Accounts**
- Enter a purchase bill, change its amount, and show the edit log with the old value, the new value, the user and the time. Then show there is no setting that turns the log off. ([audit trail](/erp/requirements#accounts-audit-trail))
- If your turnover is above ₹5 crore: generate an IRN for a test invoice and show the QR code on the print. ([e-invoice](/erp/requirements#accounts-e-invoice))
- Lock last month and try to edit an invoice in it. ([period lock](/erp/requirements#accounts-period-lock))
- If Tally stays: approve an invoice, find the voucher in TallyPrime, delete it there, and show it flagged after the next sync. ([Tally posting](/erp/requirements#accounts-tally-posting))

**Stores**
- Receive two units of the same item with different quantities and show each with its own label. ([unit-level stock](/erp/requirements#stores-unit-level))
- Reserve a unit for one order, then try to ship it on another. ([reservations](/erp/requirements#stores-reservations))
- Show the movements behind one item's balance, and that they add up to it exactly. ([derived balances](/erp/requirements#stores-balances-derived))

**Purchase**
- Receive less than ordered, enter the bill for the full quantity, and show the mismatch flagged before approval. ([three-way match](/erp/requirements#purchase-three-way-match))
- Mark a supplier as a micro enterprise and show its bills with due dates. ([MSME](/erp/requirements#purchase-msme-due-dates))

**Production**
- Import one of your real BOM sheets and show how each unmatched line is handled. ([BOM import](/erp/requirements#production-bom-import))
- Cut a plate and show the remnant back in stock with its weight. ([remnants](/erp/requirements#production-cutting-remnants))

**Access and reliability**
- Sign in as staff and open a bank page directly by its address. It should refuse. ([role access](/erp/requirements#nonfunctional-role-access))
- Pull the network cable during a sync and show what happens to the queued entries. ([offline](/erp/requirements#nonfunctional-offline))
- Ask for a full export of the demo data and open it in Excel. ([data export](/erp/requirements#nonfunctional-data-export))

**AI**
- Ask the assistant this month's sales, then compare its answer with the sales report. A number that doesn't match is the answer to whether you can trust it. ([assistant](/erp/requirements#reporting-assistant-no-invented-numbers); the full set of tests for an AI assistant is in the [AI assistant vendor test](/ai-assistant/vendor-test))

## What won't a demo tell me?

Ownership, data export and the other contract terms. Some answers only come in writing:

- **Who owns the code**, and what you hold if you stop paying. See the [contract checklist](/erp/contract-checklist).
- **How changes are priced** after the contract is signed.
- **Support response time**, and who else could take the system over.
- **A reference customer** like you, whom you call yourself.

## What are the red flags in an ERP demo?

Promises without a test, and answers that only come later:

- "That's on the roadmap" for a Must line.
- A demo only on the vendor's own sample company.
- "It's configurable" without configuring it in front of you.
- An AI feature that can't show where its numbers came from.
- No written answer on code ownership or data export.

## Where can I try these tests on a live system?

On Ahrom Labs' demos: every test above can be tried there today, with sample data that resets nightly: [manufacturing](https://boiler-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo), [trading](https://electronics-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo) and [interiors](https://interiors-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo). Use them to see what a pass looks like before you watch anyone else's demo.

title: AI in ERP: what it can safely do today
answer: AI in an ERP is safe and useful today in three jobs: answering questions from your own records through fixed, read-only look-ups; reading documents such as invoices and purchase orders into drafts a person checks; and drafting suggestions a person approves. It isn't safe yet letting a model post entries, set prices or commit dates by itself, because a model can be confidently wrong. Judge any "AI ERP" by what it may change without a person, and how it proves its numbers.
description: AI in ERP explained for owners: the three safe uses today, what not to let it do alone, AI-native claims, and how to test any ERP's AI before buying.

image.alt: A brass desk lamp lighting an open steel card-index drawer, one card raised: finding the one right record.

body:
## What can AI safely do in an ERP today?

Three jobs: answering questions from the records, reading documents into drafts a person approves, and drafting suggestions that stay read-only until someone accepts them.

| Job | What it looks like | What keeps it safe |
|---|---|---|
| **Answering questions** | "Who owes us money?", "Which orders are late?" in plain words | The model only picks the question; code runs a [fixed look-up](/systems/fixed-look-up) and a [grounding check](/systems/grounding-check) drops any sentence with a number not in the result ([how it works](/ai-assistant/how-it-works)) |
| **Reading documents** | Supplier invoices, purchase orders, freight bills and bank statements turned into draft entries | Every draft goes through a person before it is posted |
| **Drafting suggestions** | A likely match, a reorder list, a draft reply, a task | The suggestion is read-only until someone accepts it |

These are not hypothetical. Our assistants Atelier AI, Ohm AI and Ember AI answer from live business records this way, and Datum AI does the same on the construction demo's sample records ([the question library](/ai-assistant/questions) lists every question and whether it's live), and in LS Technologies' system, an electronic components trader's, 88–95% of extracted documents need no correction depending on the type, and every one is still reviewed before it is posted ([AI extraction with a person in the loop](/notes/ai-extraction-human-in-the-loop)).

## What should AI never do alone in an ERP?

Anything that changes the books or commits the business:

- **Post accounting entries.** An entry that's 99% right is a wrong ledger. Extraction drafts; a person approves.
- **Set prices or quote.** Pricing rules belong in code you can read; AI can draft the inputs, such as quantities read from a drawing.
- **Commit dates or schedule machines.** A schedule has hard limits (machine hours, routing order, material on hand) that a rule or solver can guarantee and a language model can't ([where AI fits in scheduling](/manufacturing/production-scheduling-software)).
- **Decide on documents that carry your name to a customer or inspector.** Even a very accurate suggestion should wait for a person there. We run two matchers with the same scoring, one that auto-applies and one that never does, for exactly that reason ([same confidence, different autonomy](/notes/same-confidence-different-autonomy)).

The rule of thumb: AI drafts and explains; code and people decide anything that changes a record.

## What does "AI-native ERP" actually mean?

On its own, very little; three questions about it tell you more. Vendors now describe ERPs as AI-native, AI-first or agentic. The label tells you little. Three questions tell you a lot:

1. **What can the AI change without a person?** Listing, drafting and answering are low risk. Posting, ordering and emailing customers are not.
2. **Where do its numbers come from?** A model writing its own database queries, or summarising rows, will occasionally produce a figure that's nearly right ([AI hallucination](/systems/ai-hallucination)). A fixed look-up gives the same figure as the report every time.
3. **What happens when it doesn't know?** A good assistant says "the data doesn't have that". A weak one answers anyway.

## How do I test an ERP's AI before buying?

Bring your own questions and your own documents to the demo:

- Ask five questions you already know the answers to from your reports, and compare every number. The [number check](/ai-assistant/number-check) flags any figure in an answer that isn't in the source data.
- Ask it to mark an invoice paid or delete an order. Nothing should change without a person pressing save.
- Give it a supplier invoice it hasn't seen and look at what it gets wrong, not what it gets right.
- Ask something the system can't know, like next month's demand from a customer who hasn't ordered.

The full list, with what passing and failing looks like, is in [how to test an AI assistant before you buy it](/ai-assistant/vendor-test). For choosing the ERP underneath, see [ERP for job shops](/manufacturing/job-shop-erp).

title: AI assistant for construction contractors: what it answers
answer: A contractor's assistant should answer whether each site is making money, which sites haven't sent today's report, what material is in the godown and at each site, which running bills are waiting and who owes money, all from the contractor's own records and matching its screens. Datum AI does this in the system built for a construction contractor, not yet live there, which anyone can try on the public demo with sample data, and refuses site staff the money, margin and payroll questions.
description: An AI assistant for construction contractors: the site, material, billing and labour questions it should answer from your own records, and how to check it.
body:
A contractor's work is spread over sites: daily reports from each one, material in the godown and on site, machines moving between them, labour, site cash, and running bills that wait weeks to be certified. The director's questions cut across all of it: is this site making money, who hasn't reported today, who owes us and how late. An assistant earns its place if it answers those in one line, with the same figures as the screens.

## What should it answer?

Every question Datum AI answers is listed below, with the screen to check each answer against. They cover one site end to end, margin against the estimate, daily reports filed and missing, material used against the BOQ norm, stock by location, idle machines, site cash, running-account bills and receivables by age, the cash book and the bank, attendance, KYC and gate passes, the wage register, and the trading desk's orders and supplier rates.

## What should it refuse?

Advice, changes to records, and anything a login can't see on the screens. A site engineer asking whether a site is making money should get a refusal, not a margin; "mark the bill paid" should get a pointer to the Billing tab, not a changed bill.

## How does Datum AI do it?

Datum AI is the assistant in the system built for a construction contractor, a waterproofing and repair contractor that also trades construction chemicals; it is not yet live there, so today it answers on the demo's sample records. A small model picks one of its [fixed look-ups](/systems/fixed-look-up); code runs it with the same maths as the screens, so a site's margin is the Dashboard's margin and an RA bill's amount is the Billing tab's. Site engineers and storekeepers get the site questions but not company money, margins or payroll. "Remind me to call them on Friday" drafts a task that is saved only when the person presses Save. [How it works](/ai-assistant/how-it-works) sets out the design.

You can ask it two questions yourself on the [construction demo](https://construction-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo), from any sample login, with sample sites, workers and bills.

## How do I check a vendor's assistant?

Run the [vendor test](/ai-assistant/vendor-test) on a copy of your own sites, and paste its written answers into the [number check](/ai-assistant/number-check) with the dashboard beside them. Ask about one site's margin, then work it out by hand from its approved work, material, labour and site cash: the two should match.

title: What an AI assistant sends out, and the data laws that apply
answer: Ask what is sent to the AI provider with each question. It is one of three things: the question only, the question with the rows of the answer, or your records themselves. Ahrom Labs' assistants send the question only by default. In India the DPDP Act keeps the business responsible for safeguards, breach notice and erasure, including at its AI provider, from May 2027; in the US, state privacy laws and the FTC set the rules.
description: What an AI assistant sends to the AI provider with each question, and what India's DPDP Act and US privacy rules expect of the business.
